articles.title: 2026 NFL Preseason Week 2 Winners and Losers
articles.summary: In Week 2 of the NFL preseason, top rotational players decided their fate on depth charts, for better or worse.
articles.body:
In Week 2 of the NFL preseason, top rotational players decided their fate on depth charts, for better or worse.

Most teams play fringe roster players in the final exhibition contest, so in the previous slate of games, there was a lot at stake in terms of roster pecking order.

Let's take a look at the biggest winners and losers from Week 2 of the preseason.

Many of whom have either cemented their position on the depth chart with a strong showing or jeopardized their standing following a poor performance.

Winner: Jacob Cowing, WR, San Francisco 49ers

Fringe roster players can solidify their spot on the 53-man roster with standout special teams plays. In competition for one of the last wide receiver positions on the San Francisco 49ers depth chart, Jacob Cowing made a strong case to be the team's primary punt returner.

Cowing missed the entire 2025 season because of a hamstring injury. Though he's a fourth-round pick from the 2024 draft, he needed to bounce back in his third year within the 49ers' revamped receiver room.

If Cowing secures a prominent role on special teams, he could bump free-agent acquisition Christian Kirk off the depth chart.

At training camp, Kirk has missed significant time because of a calf strain. He has minimal experience on special teams, which may work against him when San Francisco pares down its roster.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters that Cowing hasn't earned the punt-returner position, but he's "making it easier" on a forthcoming decision.

The Las Vegas Raiders pulled off a 22-20 comeback victory over the Houston Texans, but head coach Klint Kubiak wasn't satisfied with his wide receiver group. He saw regression in the unit.

"We have to get a lot better very fast," Kubiak said about the receivers via Raiders Wire Levi Damien . "We took a step backwards. Doesn't mean we can't go forward, but right now we are trying to find someone that is accountable and can help us on Sunday. Still looking."

Rookie sixth-rounder Malik Benson generated buzz at camp and caught two passes for 26 yards in the Raiders' preseason opener. Last Thursday, he had a bad drop, and Texans cornerback Tremon Smith knocked the ball out of his hands on another incompletion.

Tre Tucker didn't suit up. Jack Bech saw limited action. Jalen Nailor only caught one of his three targets.

The Raiders need quality depth at receiver to complement star tight end Brock Bowers. Thus far, Kubiak hasn't seen enough from that group. If that doesn't change by the end of next week, the Raiders may look to sign or trade for a receiver after the roster cuts deadline.

Winner: John Metchie III, WR, Carolina Panthers

John Metchie III gained momentum going into the Carolina Panthers' Week 2 preseason game.

According to Darin Gantt and Kassidy Hill of the team's official website, the Panthers mixed Metchie into the first-team offense, and he made plays during joint practices with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

In Friday's exhibition outing, Metchie led the team with six receptions for 77 receiving yards. Coming into the contest, he had a good chance of making the roster with rookie third-rounder Chris Brazzell II out for the season.

Third-year wideout Xavier Legette didn't suit up for the game because of an ankle injury.

"He got his ankle twisted up," Canales said via Anthony Rizzuti of Panthers Wire. "He has some soreness in his foot. So, we evaluated him. Right now, we're just gonna get him back going little by little. And hopefully, we'll see him at the end of this week."

If Legette's injury lingers, Metchie could carve out a role in three-receiver sets alongside 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker. Because of the Panthers' injuries at the position, he's almost certain to make the roster after signing a one-year, $1.9 million deal in March.

Loser: Mekhi Blackmon, CB, Indianapolis Colts

In two exhibition outings, Mekhi Blackmon has drawn four penalties. This week, the Atlanta Falcons declined one of his infractions and accepted the other—a pass interference on fourth down deep inside the Indianapolis Colts' red zone.

Last August, Indianapolis acquired Blackmon from the Minnesota Vikings. He started 11 of 17 games in the 2025 regular season, logging seven pass breakups and two interceptions while allowing an 86.9 passer rating in coverage.

Yet Blackmon's recent gaffes may knock him out of the rotation on the boundary if the Colts need a fill-in for cornerback Charvarius Ward, who's out indefinitely because of a back injury.

While you would assume the Colts would plug Blackmon back into a lead position opposite Sauce Gardner, his preseason struggles with ill-timed penalties should give the team pause on that idea.

In 2025, the New York Jets defense didn't record an interception, a historic low for any NFL franchise.

Safety Andre Cisco snapped the interception drought with a takeaway in the second quarter of last Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. On the Jets' following defensive drive, cornerback Samuel Womack III also picked off a pass from Will Howard.

You can say the ball bounced in the Jets' favor, or they simply took advantage of an inexperienced second-year quarterback who was a sixth-round pick. Either way, the defensive unit needed a confidence-builder in the takeaways department heading into the regular season.

Cisco and Womack were on the roster that didn't record an interception last year, though the Jets revamped their secondary with the addition of Minkah Fitzpatrick, Dane Belton, Nahshon Wright, rookie second-rounder D'Angelo Ponds and rookie seventh-rounder VJ Payne this offseason.

This year, defensive-minded head coach Aaron Glenn should have a more productive unit in terms of forced turnovers.

Loser: Deshaun Watson, QB, Cleveland Browns

While on 92.3 The Fan, Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken provided a timeline for when he'll name his starting signal-caller.

"I do not anticipate the QB decision going past early of next week," he said.

In the second half of Saturday's game against the Buffalo Bills, Deshaun Watson significantly hurt his case for the lead position. He went 5-of-12 passing for 36 yards and an interception and ran for 13 yards.

Shedeur Sanders had a better showing, completing nine of 11 passes for 74 yards, a touchdown and an interception. On his turnover, he threw a pass slightly behind tight end Jermaine Terry, and the ball bounced off him and into safety Damar Hamlin's hands.

Still, Sanders clearly outplayed Watson, which may have a lasting impression on Monken's forthcoming call on QB1.

So far in the preseason, Sanders has thrown two interceptions, but he's also recorded the Browns' lone touchdown pass in this preseason battle.

Winner: Ty Robinson, DT, Philadelphia Eagles

Ty Robinson has been one of the Philadelphia Eagles' top defensive standouts in the preseason. In two outings, he's recorded six tackles (all solo) and three sacks.

The Eagles know how to draft and develop interior defensive linemen.

Along with former first-rounders Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter, 2023 seventh-rounder Moro Ojomo has shown signs of promise, logging six sacks last season. A fourth-rounder from last year's draft. Robinson could help solidify one of the league's best defensive fronts.

In 2025, Robinson played only 15 percent of the defensive snaps across 11 outings. Barring injuries, he'll remain a backup, but the 25-year-old could find a way onto the field on pass-rushing downs.

Loser: Tyrone Tracy Jr., RB, New York Giants

Over the last two weeks, Tyrone Tracy Jr.'s stock has plummeted. In the New York Giants' preseason opener, he missed a block that allowed Minnesota Vikings safety Jay Ward to crush quarterback Jaxson Dart on a sack.

In this week's game against the Miami Dolphins, Tracy lost a fumble before halftime. He finished with six carries for 26 yards. Devin Singletary outperformed him, logging eight carries for 40 yards and a touchdown.

While this may seem like an overreaction, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Giants move on from Tracy.

Big Blue signed Narris Harris, a 6'1", 232-pound ball-carrier who can split early-down touches with Cam Skattebo. Singletary may have played his way into the No. 3 spot. Tracy is the most dynamic pass-catcher of the group, but if the Giants believe he's a liability in pass protection, they may cut or trade him.

Winner: Joe Milton III, QB, Dallas Cowboys

The Dallas Cowboys ran the ball effectively against the Arizona Cardinals, thanks in large part to running back Jaydon Blue's 15 carries for 75 yards. He made a strong case to surpass Malik Davis for the No. 2 spot behind Javonte Williams.

That said, in a battle with Sam Howell for the primary backup quarterback job, Joe Milton III had a statement performance. He threw for 179 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for a score.

Milton's arm strength has drawn oohs and aahs when he takes the field, but he was accurate last Saturday night, completing nine of 13 passes.

By the way, Howell threw an interception in the red zone midway through the fourth quarter. Dallas signed him to a one-year, $2.5 million deal in March. Heading into the final week of the preseason, he's behind Milton in the pecking order.

Last offseason, the Kansas City Chiefs signed Jaylon Moore to a two-year, $30 million deal. Based on that contract, he's the probable full-time starter at right tackle after lining up on both sides of the line in the previous season.

However, the Chiefs should continue to look for upgrades at right tackle. Moore didn't look impressive in Week 2 of the preseason against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

On X, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame best described the fifth-year pro's pass-blocking performance.

"Jaylon Moore is barely touching the edge rushers. He looks like he's in cement."

Khalil Benson didn't look any better against the Buccaneers' pass rush. Bleacher Report scout Daniel Harms provided his insight on the undrafted rookie's Saturday outing.

"Much rougher outing for Khalil Benson tonight," Harms posted. "Definitely looks better as a run blocker but the pass pro is not great," Harms wrote in a follow-up post .

With quarterback Patrick Mahomes in line to return from an ACL tear, the Chiefs must be careful about who they field to protect him. If Moore can't handle edge-rushers in the preseason, he could have a rough campaign in a lead role.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

While this may seem like an overreaction, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Giants move on from Tracy.

Big Blue signed Narris Harris, a 6'1", 232-pound ball-carrier who can split early-down touches with Cam Skattebo. Singletary may have played his way into the No. 3 spot. Tracy is the most dynamic pass-catcher of the group, but if the Giants believe he's a liability in pass protection, they may cut or trade him.
Winner: Joe Milton III, QB, Dallas Cowboys

The Dallas Cowboys ran the ball effectively against the Arizona Cardinals, thanks in large part to running back Jaydon Blue's 15 carries for 75 yards. He made a strong case to surpass Malik Davis for the No. 2 spot behind Javonte Williams.
That said, in a battle with Sam Howell for the primary backup quarterback job, Joe Milton III had a statement performance. He threw for 179 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for a score.
Milton's arm strength has drawn oohs and aahs when he takes the field, but he was accurate last Saturday night, completing nine of 13 passes.

By the way, Howell threw an interception in the red zone midway through the fourth quarter. Dallas signed him to a one-year, $2.5 million deal in March. Heading into the final week of the preseason, he's behind Milton in the pecking order.

Last offseason, the Kansas City Chiefs signed Jaylon Moore to a two-year, $30 million deal. Based on that contract, he's the probable full-time starter at right tackle after lining up on both sides of the line in the previous season.
However, the Chiefs should continue to look for upgrades at right tackle. Moore didn't look impressive in Week 2 of the preseason against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
On X, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame best described the fifth-year pro's pass-blocking performance.
"Jaylon Moore is barely touching the edge rushers. He looks like he's in cement."
Khalil Benson didn't look any better against the Buccaneers' pass rush. Bleacher Report scout Daniel Harms provided his insight on the undrafted rookie's Saturday outing.
"Much rougher outing for Khalil Benson tonight," Harms posted. "Definitely looks better as a run blocker but the pass pro is not great," Harms wrote in a follow-up post .

With quarterback Patrick Mahomes in line to return from an ACL tear, the Chiefs must be careful about who they field to protect him. If Moore can't handle edge-rushers in the preseason, he could have a rough campaign in a lead role.
Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Christian McCaffrey Injury Update, Latest on 49ers' Star's Practice Status Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: After sitting out a string of practices due to an undisclosed injury, San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey appears to have recovered.
articles.body:
After sitting out a string of practices due to an undisclosed injury, San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey appears to have recovered.

McCaffrey was seen in uniform for Sunday's training camp practice, and he later participated in individual drills:

McCaffrey spoke about his situation after practice:

McCaffrey's return wasn't the only positive injury news in San Francisco. Star tight end George Kittle was activated from the physically unable to perform list on Sunday, marking the most significant step in his return from a torn right Achilles. The 32-year-old has been targeting a Week 1 return, though he acknowledged that he could miss some time to start the year.

"I want to play in every football game that I possibly can play in, but I'm also aware it's an 18-week season," Kittle said earlier this month. "If you miss Week 1 and you're playing Week 2, hey, it is what it is. … I'm just going to keep that as my goal, and then we'll adjust from there if we need to."

As for McCaffrey, he was sidelined for nearly three weeks with what was described as "tightness" with no other explanation. He and Kittle sat out team drills on Sunday as they were eased back into the swing of things. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said last week that McCaffrey would be active if it were the regular season.

"I think if it wasn't Christian and we were in a game week, I think he would play today," Shanahan said.

The 49ers are hoping to return to title contention this season, so having their veterans healthy will be the key to competing against the elite teams in the NFC.

articles.title: Cowboys' Shiyazh Pete Gives Inspirational Locker-Room Speech in Viral Video After NFL Preseason Game
articles.summary: Following the Dallas Cowboys' 34-13 preseason road win over the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday, offensive tackle Shiyazh Pete delivered a stirring speech to his Cowboys teammates.
articles.body:
Following the Dallas Cowboys' 34-13 preseason road win over the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday, offensive tackle Shiyazh Pete delivered a stirring speech to his Cowboys teammates.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer noted that he had never seen an entire cheering section for a singular player during a preseason game before, but because Pete had exactly that at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, he allowed Pete to break the team down in the locker room:

Expressing gratitude and pride to play for the Cowboys, Pete said, "This game, this star, this team will make us brothers."

Pete, who is originally from Montana and played collegiately at New Mexico State and Kentucky, is a member of the Navajo Native American tribe. A large contingent of Native Americans were in attendance for Saturday's game, and they gave him a warm reception, per Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News .

The Cowboys signed Pete as an undrafted free agent in April, and he has been making his case for a roster spot throughout training camp and the preseason.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Latest ADP for Top Sleepers and Tips to Strategize
articles.summary: With Week 2 of the NFL preseason set to wrap on Sunday, time is running out for fantasy managers to cram pre-draft preparation. Fortunately, this year's exhibition games have given managers a glimpse of some potential sleepers to target in the middle and late rounds.
articles.body:
With Week 2 of the NFL preseason set to wrap on Sunday, time is running out for fantasy managers to cram pre-draft preparation. Fortunately, this year's exhibition games have given managers a glimpse of some potential sleepers to target in the middle and late rounds.

It's always important to remember that championship fantasy rosters aren't built on top draft picks alone—though early busts can certainly derail an otherwise promising campaign.

Here, you'll find a few tips for targeting sleepers during the draft, along with a few upward-trending players. We'll dive into why these players could provide great value in 2026 and examine their current average draft positions (ADP).

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Preparation and accurate projections are the key to uncovering value at any stage of a fantasy draft. Top-tier players like Ja'Marr Chase and Bijan Robinson are targeted at the very top because managers know they'll have a high-volume role and can project elite production, provided they stay healthy.

Accurately projecting sleepers is a little trickier; otherwise they wouldn't be sleepers at all. The trick is to use all of the available information—including practice reports, preseason film study, depth charts, and supporting casts—to make educated guesses regarding roles.

For example, we know that rookie running back Jadarian Price is likely to see a fairly heavy workload for the Seattle Seahawks early in 2026. He's listed behind George Holani on Seattle's depth chart . However, he has a high-volume skill set and won't initially compete for touches with Zach Charbonnet, who is recovering from a torn ACL that he suffered in mid-January.

With an ADP of 69, Price isn't a true sleeper but could significantly outperform his draft position. Holani, meanwhile, is a legitimate sleeper with an ADP of 260 . He's likely to have more value early in the year, but he's worth picking up late in drafts.

It's also important to prepare a draft strategy ahead of time in order to target sleepers in the correct range. If you're planning on a zero-RB build, for example, you'll likely want to jump on RB sleepers a couple of rounds earlier than you might target WRs and TEs. Any time you're banking on middle- or late-round value at a position, you cannot afford to miss.

Even with sleepers, it's better to make a move a round early than a round too late.

Of course, it's equally important to have a plan for pivoting. Just because you plan to target a specific position at a set stage in the draft, that doesn't mean other managers will cooperate. If an early run on receivers leaves second-tier RBs available in the middle rounds, it's probably worth abandoning that zero-RB approach, taking a back or two before moving on to WR, TE, and QB sleepers.

Lastly, it's critical to remember that roster building doesn't end with the draft. If your draft is being held, say, a week ahead of August 30 roster cuts, there's a very good chance that a few roles and situations will change after you've made your initial selections.

Don't be afraid to drop a late-round pick or two in order to snap up sleeper talent you trust off the waiver wire.

Quarterback Kyler Murray is currently trending as a mid-level streaming option, at best. His ADP puts him well behind signal-callers like Bo Nix, Jaxson Dart, and Brock Purdy, which is curious.

There's a lot of opportunity here for managers willing to take a flier on Murray. He has a dangerous dual-threat skill set and has played at a Pro Bowl level in the past. He has also been named the Minnesota Vikings' starter already, which means managers have some clarity about his initial 2026 role.

Additionally, Murray has a terrific supporting cast, led by Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Jauan Jennings. In Kevin O'Connell's offense, he'll have a chance to approach career-best numbers. He's also poised to outperform his ADP by a large margin.

We don't have as much clarity on the 2026 role for Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey. He's listed behind J.K. Dobbins on Denver's depth chart and could also lose touches to rookie fourth-round pick Jonah Coleman .

However, we can project that Harvey will have a significant role with a good amount of upside. In a committee role as a 2025 rookie, he caught 47 passes, tallied 896 scrimmage yards, and scored 12 touchdowns. Given Dobbins' lengthy injury history, he'll have a real chance to top those numbers in 2026.

Harvey's ADP currently has him trending as a fifth- or sixth-round pick and somewhere in the early 30s among running backs. However, he finished last season as RB20 and could finish higher this year, which means he's being undervalued.

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

Michael Pittman Jr., WR, Pittsburgh Steelers

Wideout Michael Pittman Jr. was traded from the Indianapolis Colts to the Pittsburgh Steelers this offseason. He'll now serve as the No. 2 receiver opposite DK Metcalf after serving as a complement to Alec Pierce.

Managers seem to be discounting Pittman's floor because of either A.) Metcalf's presence or B.)the lackluster offense Pittsburgh produced last season. His ADP has Pittman trending in the mid-30s among WR, even though he finished last season as WR18.

Pittman should have a good chance to match last year's production, even with a change of scenery. Aaron Rodgers is still pretty good at distributing the football, and the Steelers don't have a lot of receiver depth behind Pittman and Metcalf.

With new head coach Mike McCarthy likely to give Pittsburgh's offense a spark, Pittman should be targeted earlier than he currently is.

*Fantasy scoring and ADP from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty Injury Update, Latest on Raiders Star After Exiting Practice Ahead of NFL Season
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders and Ashton Jeanty might have avoided the worst-case scenario.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders and Ashton Jeanty might have avoided the worst-case scenario.

Despite a scary injury at practice Sunday, Jeanty has reportedly been diagnosed with a sprained ankle, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . It is "not considered a long-term injury," per Schefter, although the timetable is not yet known.

Vincent Bonsignore of the California Post was among those who reported Jeanty injured his leg in practice and could not put pressure on it as he left the field.

Raiders players "took a knee and said a prayer after Jeanty exited the field," according to ESPN's Ryan McFadden .

Jeanty suffered the injury when he dove for a catch and landed awkwardly on his right leg during team drills, according to McFadden. He was helped off the field by trainers. McFadden added that the Raiders declined to comment on Jeanty's status at this time.

The No. 6 pick in the 2025 draft, Jeanty started all 17 games for the Raiders as a rookie and recorded 266 carries for 975 yards and five touchdowns. He also added 55 receptions for 346 yards and five more scores.

Earlier this month, McFadden reported that Jeanty "has looked extremely comfortable in this outside zone scheme" instituted by first-year head coach Klint Kubiak. He reportedly "has had multiple explosive runs down the sidelines during practice," and Kubiak wanted him to be "a bell-cow running back."

The Raiders added depth to their running back room when they selected Mike Washington Jr. in the fourth round of this year's draft. The rookie has totaled 119 yards in two preseason games, and McFadden noted that he "has shown that he could be a major factor."

Still, it's safe to say that the Raiders will be hoping for the best for Jeanty, as he was expected to take a leap in his sophomore campaign.

articles.title: Buying or Selling the Top NFL Performers of Preseason Week 2
articles.summary: Though it didn't bring as much excitement as the regular season ultimately will, Week 2 of the NFL preseason was quite a bit of fun. Not every game was competitive, of course, but the most recent slate of exhibition games brought some thrilling standout performances.
articles.body:
Though it didn't bring as much excitement as the regular season ultimately will, Week 2 of the NFL preseason was quite a bit of fun. Not every game was competitive, of course, but the most recent slate of exhibition games brought some thrilling standout performances.

Of course, it's important to consume strong preseason performances with a grain of salt. Players are rarely playing with or against a full complement of starters and are frequently operating in the most basic of schemes. Some performances, while impressive, prove to be a mirage.

Last year, for example, Chris Blair led the NFL in preseason receiving yards and went on to play a mere 12 offensive snaps for the Atlanta Falcons.

Here, we'll dive into some of the biggest standout performances of preseason Week 2 and buy or sell each outing based on factors like game situations, past performances, projected 2026 role, and overall player expectations.

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III had a fantastic outing against a bad Arizona Cardinals defense, finishing with 179 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and a rushing score. He also made several eye-catching throws on Saturday evening.

However, the Cowboys are still leaving the competition for their backup QB job open for now.

"This is long from over," head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after the game (h/t ProFootballTalk's Josh Alper ).

However, Milton's Week 2 display should be enough to earn him the nod over Sam Howell to be Dak Prescott's understudy. The 2024 sixth-round pick out of Tennessee has long possessed impressive physical traits, and he's beginning to add some nuance, anticipation, and processing to his game.

The fact that Milton's latest performance came against an Arizona team that seemed largely uninterested in playing defense should not diminish his development. His combination of arm talent and running ability makes him a much better fit for Dallas' offense than Howell should either be called upon to play in the regular season.

Sell: Carson Steele, RB, Philadelphia Eagles

Milton wasn't the only NFC East backup to put on a show on Saturday. Philadelphia Eagles backup running back Carson Steele dropped jaws with not one, but two, instances of leaping over a defender.

His second hurdle came en route to the end zone and a go-ahead fourth-quarter score.

Steele finished with 33 rushing yards, 84 receiving yards, and the touchdown against the New England Patriots on Saturday. Was his outing a sign that the Eagles have a new offensive weapon who can spell Saquon Barkley?

Not exactly. While Steele certainly has the talent to provide depth behind Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley, he has never been a particularly efficient player in the NFL. He averaged just 3.3 yards per carry with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and spent the next season on their practice squad.

The 6'0", 228-pound Steele may stick with Philly as an option at fullback, but he's going to be an offensive afterthought once the Eagles get to the regular season.

Buy: De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

During April's draft, the San Francisco 49ers traded down twice before taking Mississippi wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling 33rd overall.

While some viewed the selection as a reach—and, to be fair, Stribling was the 68th-ranked player on the Bleacher Report Scouting Department's final big board —the rookie is looking like a strong fit for San Francisco's offense.

During Thursday's 41-17 romp over the Los Angeles Chargers, Stribling tied for the team lead (with KhaDarel Hodge) in receptions and receiving yards while showcasing some big-play ability.

This marked the second strong preseason outing for Stribling, who had seven catches for 63 yards in San Francisco's preseason opener.

It would be silly to put too much stock in a receiver's numbers against backups and vanilla defenses. However, Stribling is probably poised for a strong rookie season. His combination of size (6'2", 207 lbs) and speed (4.36-second 40-yard dash) makes him well-suited for Kyle Shanahan's spacing-based passing attack, and it's not as if the 49ers are loaded with healthy receiver depth.

It's too early to be penciling in Stribling for Offensive Rookie of the Year. However, he should be walking into a substantial role, and it's not too early for 49ers fans to be excited about it.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Sell: Colbie Young, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

Like Stribling, Cincinnati Bengals fourth-round pick Colbie Young is ready to have an instant impact as a rookie, right? Based on his performance on Saturday night, one might believe so.

The 6'4", 218-pound Georgia product logged three catches and led the Bengals with 48 receiving yards. He also used his size and ball skills to show what sort of red-zone threat he could be for Cincinnati.

However, while Stribling is likely to have a big role right away in San Francisco, Young will probably tumble down the depth chart once the regular season begins.

Sure, having a tall, big-bodied receiver can be beneficial near the goal line. However, the Bengals already have premium red-zone targets in Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, and Mike Gesicki. The reality is that Young just isn't likely to see many opportunities in Cincinnati's offense this season.

Let's not forget that Mitchell Tinsley was a Bengals preseason darling in 2025, due in large part to his ability to make contested catches. He went on to record just eight receptions in the regular season.

Geno Smith officially made his New York Jets return on Friday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. While it's certainly worth noting that he primarily battled backups, his command of the offense and near-perfection during limited action is also noteworthy.

Smith was a perfect 7-of-7 on his lone drive against Pittsburgh, which he finished with a touchdown pass.

Now, look. We're talking about the Jets, and they're seemingly not allowed to have nice things at quarterback, so it's fair to be skeptical of Smith's performance. However, fans shouldn't be shocked if he makes the offense a lot of fun in 2026.

Smith was a two-time Pro Bowler with the Seattle Seahawks, and he's a great fit for Frank Reich's offense. Had he not spent last season on the sinking ship that was the Pete Carroll-led Las Vegas Raiders, Smith would probably be carrying much higher expectations in New York.

While Smith isn't going to be an MVP candidate or lead the Jets to the Super Bowl, he should perform well with a supporting cast now headlined by Olumuyiwa Fashanu, Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, Kenyon Sadiq , and Omar Cooper Jr.

Sell: Shedeur Sanders, QB, Cleveland Browns

Editor's Note: The Browns named Deshaun Watson the starting QB on Monday.

While Smith is flying under the radar in New York, everything that Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders does seems to be magnified.

The second-year signal-caller out of Colorado was far from perfect against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday. However, he was largely solid while going 9-of-11 for 74 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

Sanders fans will be quick to point out that his interception was deflected out of his intended target's hands while his touchdown strike was on time and accurate.

However, a couple of mostly-good series against Buffalo backups doesn't mean that Sanders is ready to lead Cleveland to the postseason. It might not even be enough to put Sanders ahead of Deshaun Watson in the QB competition—even if Watson has become a frustratingly low bar to clear.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Browns plan to announce their Week 1 starter on Monday.

The difference between Smith and Sanders is that only one has shown that he can play at a consistently high level over the course of an NFL season. Sanders has only shown flashes, and while he could still develop into a quality starter for Cleveland, he's a long way away from being a franchise quarterback or making the Browns forget about the 2027 quarterback class.

Buy: Mike Washington, RB, Las Vegas Raiders

All eyes have been on Raiders quarterback and first overall pick Fernando Mendoza this summer, but he hasn't been the only Las Vegas rookie generating a bit of buzz. Fourth-round running back Mike Washington Jr. has flashed in practices and turned a few heads against the Houston Texans on Thursday.

Washington caught a pair of passes, logged a team-high 56 rushing yards, and continued to show his big-play ability.

Through two preseason games, Washington has racked up 119 rushing yards while averaging an impressive 7.9 yards per carry. Now, it's worth noting that his average has been significantly boosted by some long runs, but he's still been one of the preseason's most impressive ball-carriers.

The question, of course, is whether Las Vegas will have a role for Washington with 2025 first-round pick Ashton Jeanty leading the backfield. In all likelihood, it will.

New head coach Klint Kubiak used a committee approach as the Seahawks' offensive coordinator, and Washington's breakaway speed (4.33-second 40-yard dash) should make him an excellent complement to Jeanty.

And Washington can be more than just a speedy change of pace, as evidenced by the 28 receptions and 1,296 scrimmage yards he logged last season at Arkansas. Las Vegas may lean on him for the immediate future, as Jeanty suffered an injury in Sunday's practice and is believed to have a sprained ankle, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Washington wasn't the only fourth-round rookie who made the highlight reel in the Raiders-Texans game.

Houston linebacker Wade Woodaz made the play of the day when he picked off Mendoza and ran it back for an 80-yard pick-six.

While Woodaz's two tackles and big play may foreshadow what is to come, fans shouldn't expect him to be a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate or an immediate IDP fantasy star.

A running back like Washington can easily slot into a specific role, especially on a rebuilding team that is hungry for talent. The Texans, however, are legitimate title contenders with two entrenched starting inside linebackers—Azeez Al-Shaair and Henry To'oTo'o—with a loaded defense overall.

Woodaz doesn't have a wide-open path to playing time, and it doesn't help that he's set to undergo surgery for a broken thumb, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston.

While Woodaz could very well become a future star for the Texans, Thursday's preseason outing may be his last big game for a while.
paragraphs: Though it didn't bring as much excitement as the regular season ultimately will, Week 2 of the NFL preseason was quite a bit of fun. Not every game was competitive, of course, but the most recent slate of exhibition games brought some thrilling standout performances.

Of course, it's important to consume strong preseason performances with a grain of salt. Players are rarely playing with or against a full complement of starters and are frequently operating in the most basic of schemes. Some performances, while impressive, prove to be a mirage.
Last year, for example, Chris Blair led the NFL in preseason receiving yards and went on to play a mere 12 offensive snaps for the Atlanta Falcons.

Here, we'll dive into some of the biggest standout performances of preseason Week 2 and buy or sell each outing based on factors like game situations, past performances, projected 2026 role, and overall player expectations.

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III had a fantastic outing against a bad Arizona Cardinals defense, finishing with 179 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and a rushing score. He also made several eye-catching throws on Saturday evening.
However, the Cowboys are still leaving the competition for their backup QB job open for now.
"This is long from over," head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after the game (h/t ProFootballTalk's Josh Alper ).

However, Milton's Week 2 display should be enough to earn him the nod over Sam Howell to be Dak Prescott's understudy. The 2024 sixth-round pick out of Tennessee has long possessed impressive physical traits, and he's beginning to add some nuance, anticipation, and processing to his game.

The fact that Milton's latest performance came against an Arizona team that seemed largely uninterested in playing defense should not diminish his development. His combination of arm talent and running ability makes him a much better fit for Dallas' offense than Howell should either be called upon to play in the regular season.
Sell: Carson Steele, RB, Philadelphia Eagles
Milton wasn't the only NFC East backup to put on a show on Saturday. Philadelphia Eagles backup running back Carson Steele dropped jaws with not one, but two, instances of leaping over a defender.
His second hurdle came en route to the end zone and a go-ahead fourth-quarter score.

Steele finished with 33 rushing yards, 84 receiving yards, and the touchdown against the New England Patriots on Saturday. Was his outing a sign that the Eagles have a new offensive weapon who can spell Saquon Barkley?

Not exactly. While Steele certainly has the talent to provide depth behind Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley, he has never been a particularly efficient player in the NFL. He averaged just 3.3 yards per carry with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and spent the next season on their practice squad.
The 6'0", 228-pound Steele may stick with Philly as an option at fullback, but he's going to be an offensive afterthought once the Eagles get to the regular season.
Buy: De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers
During April's draft, the San Francisco 49ers traded down twice before taking Mississippi wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling 33rd overall.

While some viewed the selection as a reach—and, to be fair, Stribling was the 68th-ranked player on the Bleacher Report Scouting Department's final big board —the rookie is looking like a strong fit for San Francisco's offense.
During Thursday's 41-17 romp over the Los Angeles Chargers, Stribling tied for the team lead (with KhaDarel Hodge) in receptions and receiving yards while showcasing some big-play ability.
This marked the second strong preseason outing for Stribling, who had seven catches for 63 yards in San Francisco's preseason opener.

It would be silly to put too much stock in a receiver's numbers against backups and vanilla defenses. However, Stribling is probably poised for a strong rookie season. His combination of size (6'2", 207 lbs) and speed (4.36-second 40-yard dash) makes him well-suited for Kyle Shanahan's spacing-based passing attack, and it's not as if the 49ers are loaded with healthy receiver depth.
It's too early to be penciling in Stribling for Offensive Rookie of the Year. However, he should be walking into a substantial role, and it's not too early for 49ers fans to be excited about it.
Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut
Sell: Colbie Young, WR, Cincinnati Bengals
Like Stribling, Cincinnati Bengals fourth-round pick Colbie Young is ready to have an instant impact as a rookie, right? Based on his performance on Saturday night, one might believe so.

The 6'4", 218-pound Georgia product logged three catches and led the Bengals with 48 receiving yards. He also used his size and ball skills to show what sort of red-zone threat he could be for Cincinnati.
However, while Stribling is likely to have a big role right away in San Francisco, Young will probably tumble down the depth chart once the regular season begins.

Sure, having a tall, big-bodied receiver can be beneficial near the goal line. However, the Bengals already have premium red-zone targets in Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, and Mike Gesicki. The reality is that Young just isn't likely to see many opportunities in Cincinnati's offense this season.

Let's not forget that Mitchell Tinsley was a Bengals preseason darling in 2025, due in large part to his ability to make contested catches. He went on to record just eight receptions in the regular season.

Geno Smith officially made his New York Jets return on Friday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. While it's certainly worth noting that he primarily battled backups, his command of the offense and near-perfection during limited action is also noteworthy.
Smith was a perfect 7-of-7 on his lone drive against Pittsburgh, which he finished with a touchdown pass.

Now, look. We're talking about the Jets, and they're seemingly not allowed to have nice things at quarterback, so it's fair to be skeptical of Smith's performance. However, fans shouldn't be shocked if he makes the offense a lot of fun in 2026.

Smith was a two-time Pro Bowler with the Seattle Seahawks, and he's a great fit for Frank Reich's offense. Had he not spent last season on the sinking ship that was the Pete Carroll-led Las Vegas Raiders, Smith would probably be carrying much higher expectations in New York.

While Smith isn't going to be an MVP candidate or lead the Jets to the Super Bowl, he should perform well with a supporting cast now headlined by Olumuyiwa Fashanu, Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, Kenyon Sadiq , and Omar Cooper Jr.
Sell: Shedeur Sanders, QB, Cleveland Browns
Editor's Note: The Browns named Deshaun Watson the starting QB on Monday.
While Smith is flying under the radar in New York, everything that Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders does seems to be magnified.

The second-year signal-caller out of Colorado was far from perfect against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday. However, he was largely solid while going 9-of-11 for 74 yards with one touchdown and one interception.
Sanders fans will be quick to point out that his interception was deflected out of his intended target's hands while his touchdown strike was on time and accurate.

However, a couple of mostly-good series against Buffalo backups doesn't mean that Sanders is ready to lead Cleveland to the postseason. It might not even be enough to put Sanders ahead of Deshaun Watson in the QB competition—even if Watson has become a frustratingly low bar to clear.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Browns plan to announce their Week 1 starter on Monday.

The difference between Smith and Sanders is that only one has shown that he can play at a consistently high level over the course of an NFL season. Sanders has only shown flashes, and while he could still develop into a quality starter for Cleveland, he's a long way away from being a franchise quarterback or making the Browns forget about the 2027 quarterback class.
Buy: Mike Washington, RB, Las Vegas Raiders

All eyes have been on Raiders quarterback and first overall pick Fernando Mendoza this summer, but he hasn't been the only Las Vegas rookie generating a bit of buzz. Fourth-round running back Mike Washington Jr. has flashed in practices and turned a few heads against the Houston Texans on Thursday.
Washington caught a pair of passes, logged a team-high 56 rushing yards, and continued to show his big-play ability.

Through two preseason games, Washington has racked up 119 rushing yards while averaging an impressive 7.9 yards per carry. Now, it's worth noting that his average has been significantly boosted by some long runs, but he's still been one of the preseason's most impressive ball-carriers.
The question, of course, is whether Las Vegas will have a role for Washington with 2025 first-round pick Ashton Jeanty leading the backfield. In all likelihood, it will.

New head coach Klint Kubiak used a committee approach as the Seahawks' offensive coordinator, and Washington's breakaway speed (4.33-second 40-yard dash) should make him an excellent complement to Jeanty.

And Washington can be more than just a speedy change of pace, as evidenced by the 28 receptions and 1,296 scrimmage yards he logged last season at Arkansas. Las Vegas may lean on him for the immediate future, as Jeanty suffered an injury in Sunday's practice and is believed to have a sprained ankle, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .
Washington wasn't the only fourth-round rookie who made the highlight reel in the Raiders-Texans game.
Houston linebacker Wade Woodaz made the play of the day when he picked off Mendoza and ran it back for an 80-yard pick-six.
While Woodaz's two tackles and big play may foreshadow what is to come, fans shouldn't expect him to be a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate or an immediate IDP fantasy star.

A running back like Washington can easily slot into a specific role, especially on a rebuilding team that is hungry for talent. The Texans, however, are legitimate title contenders with two entrenched starting inside linebackers—Azeez Al-Shaair and Henry To'oTo'o—with a loaded defense overall.

While Woodaz could very well become a future star for the Texans, Thursday's preseason outing may be his last big game for a while.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Beats Shedeur Sanders in Browns' QB1 Battle for NFL Week 1 vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders will begin his second season in the NFL on the bench for the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders will begin his second season in the NFL on the bench for the Cleveland Browns.

Deshaun Watson was named the team's starter over Sanders on Monday for the Sept. 13 season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added that Watson was the "favorite going into camp" ahead of Sanders and Dillon Gabriel.

The quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson was the biggest storyline surrounding the Browns during OTAs and training camp, and the veteran ended up showing new head coach Todd Monken enough to win the job.

During the early portion of OTAs in May, Monken told reporters he hoped to have a quarterback depth chart in place by training camp but also did not want to rush things. He added, "we'll have it set for Jacksonville."

Yet there were signs Watson was gradually pulling away as training camp progressed:

Watson also started the preseason opener against the Chicago Bears and played solidly while going 11-of-15 for 126 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. Sanders entered the game after him and struggled while going 6-of-11 for 79 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception.

It was Sanders who played better in the second preseason game against the Buffalo Bills by going 9-of-11 for 74 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Watson was just 5-of-12 for 36 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception.

Watson then slammed Browns fans for booing him in the aftermath:

After all the back-and-forth, the depth chart is now set for Jacksonville. That means Sanders will have to wait for the chance to improve on his rookie-year struggles.

Cleveland selected him with a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft after he surprisingly fell so far despite being the Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year in his final collegiate season. He began his rookie campaign on the bench but eventually got the opportunity to start.

While his 3-4 record in seven starts doesn't exactly jump out, the Browns were 2-8 in their other 10 games. But it's not as if Sanders led the way to that improvement with excellent individual play, as he finished with seven touchdown passes, 10 interceptions and an ugly 18.9 QBR .

Still, he flashed his potential at times and played through the inconsistency that many rookies deal with in their first NFL season. He figured to be better in 2026 with a potential second-year leap, but that will be more difficult now from a backup role.

As for Watson, the Browns certainly hope he moves past the disappointment that has defined his tenure with the team.

There was a time when he was one of the best quarterbacks in the league when he made three straight Pro Bowls for the Houston Texans from 2018-20. He also led the entire NFL with 4,823 passing yards in 2020.

Yet he has made just 19 starts since the Browns traded for him before the 2022 season due to a combination of suspension and injuries. He is 9-10 in those starts and is yet to throw for more than seven touchdowns in a single season with Cleveland.

The 2026 campaign is set to be the final one on Watson's contract with the AFC North team. Winning the starting job gives him and the Browns a chance to salvage something after the team gave up draft capital in his acquisition and then gave him a five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million deal.

But this means Sanders will have to wait for his next chance.

articles.title: Predicting When Shedeur Sanders Should Start After Deshaun Watson Wins Browns' QB1 Job vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have their starting quarterback to open the 2026 NFL season. Whether it's the last change to their QB room remains to be seen.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have their starting quarterback to open the 2026 NFL season. Whether it's the last change to their QB room remains to be seen.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday that Deshaun Watson is Cleveland's QB1 over Shedeur Sanders.

Given how Watson closed out the preseason, nobody will be shocked if he fails to hold onto the job for the entire year.

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Should coach Todd Monken decide to elevate Sanders, Week 5 is a plausible window for that to happen.

The Browns play their biggest rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers, in Week 4, and the game is on a Thursday night. The fan angst could reach a fever pitch if Cleveland suffers a tough loss, and the schedule would allow for Sanders to have a few extra days to get used to the starting role again.

It's hard to remember a Week 1 quarterback call that felt more doomed than this.

Watson wasn't convincing on the field during the Browns' first two preseason games. He went 16-of-27 for 162 yards and one interception, also losing one fumble.

His press conference after Saturday's 31-7 loss to the Buffalo Bills only turned more fans against the three-time Pro Bowler.

In Watson, the Browns have a QB who hasn't looked like a viable starter since 2020 and one who could get booed out of his home stadium whenever something goes wrong.

Granted it came with a different coaching staff, but Cleveland only waited four games before pulling the plug on Joe Flacco in 2025. Dillon Gabriel took over the offense by Week 5 last year, eventually giving way to Sanders.

The Browns' first encounter with the Steelers could present a perfect storm.

The team may be 0-3 heading into a nationally televised game. Fans in Northeast Ohio will already be growing restless as they prepare to watch a quarterback they clearly don't like on a very deep level. Imagine the atmosphere inside Huntington Bank Field if the Browns are down big in the second half and the offense is failing to move the ball.

Maybe Cleveland fares better than expected out of the gate. Nothing gets a fanbase on board more than winning.

The preseason didn't provide any evidence that's likely to happen, so those who thought Sanders should start ahead of Watson will probably get their wish sooner or later.

articles.title: Ravens Reveal 'White Noise' Jerseys in Hype Video, Fresh Photo for Saints Game on NFL Schedule
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have something special planned for their 2026 home opener against the New Orleans Saints on Sept. 20.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have something special planned for their 2026 home opener against the New Orleans Saints on Sept. 20.

The Ravens announced on Monday that after opening the 2026 season on the road against the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13, they will be donning their new "White Noise" jerseys when they return home for their Week 2 matchup against the Saints.

The Ravens updated their threads for the first time in 26 years and were among the many teams to unveil new uniform lineups this offseason.

After missing the playoffs in 2025, the Ravens are clearly bringing a new energy into the 2026 season as they try to return to postseason contention.

articles.title: The Browns, no strangers to embarrassment, reach a new low naming Deshaun Watson starting QB
articles.summary: Browns fans booed their starting quarterback in the team's last preseason game.
articles.body:
Every team has some level of optimism coming into the season. Then there's the Cleveland Browns , who voluntarily signed up for having their starting quarterback booed mercilessly throughout their home opener.

The Browns know embarrassment. They haven't won a division title since 1989. They went 0-16 in 2017, a year after going 1-15. Their list of quarterbacks since returning to the NFL in 1999 is so long and treacherous, it became a running joke .

And Monday brought a new low, even for the Browns.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

Deshaun Watson will be the team's starting quarterback in Week 1, the Browns announced. Shedeur Sanders , a younger player who definitively outplayed Watson in the second preseason game, will be the backup. Watson got booed by the home fans Saturday, then waged war with them for it , calling them disrespectful and bringing up fans cheering his Achilles injury. Despite all of that, the Browns chose Watson.

In truth, it was never a competition. We found that out Monday. Someone in the Browns decided long ago that Watson would start. They started a media blitz to ease Browns fans into that idea last December. He was going to start even though in March 2025, team owner Jimmy Haslam called the Watson trade a "big swing and miss." Nothing has changed since then. But Watson, the very definition of a sunk cost, will start the season.

Sorry, Browns fans. You deserve better than this.

Watson didn't take it well when he was booed after an interception Saturday. He said fans held a personal grudge against him. It was personal, to a degree. But he missed the point, as he has done repeatedly throughout his Browns career.

Browns fans weren't just booing Watson, with his long and sordid off-field history and the trivia answer to "worst trade ever" and also "worst contract ever." They were booing the franchise itself.

There's no logical world in which Watson should be starting Week 1. He's 30 years old. He has never played well in Cleveland. There's no trade value to be salvaged. He is obviously fed up with Cleveland, and Cleveland is fed up with him. When Browns fans booed Watson, part of that had to be letting ownership, the front office and the coaching staff know they did not want Watson playing anymore. They were done. It was a revolt. They are smart enough to know that the Browns should have moved on, even though the franchise itself didn't seem to get that.

Browns fans voiced their displeasure Saturday. They were spit on by the franchise with Monday's decision.

And if Watson thought he was booed in the preseason, just wait until their home opener in Week 3.

Browns have been setting this up for months

The weird part about the Watson ordeal is that the Browns acted like there was a competition when there now obviously wasn't. Sanders completely outplayed Watson last weekend, but afterward Browns head coach Todd Monken twisted himself into a pretzel to justify the predetermined decision to pick Watson.

"I'm not going to let one half of football, one frustrating moment dictate what our decision is going to be that we think is in the best interest of the Browns moving forward and especially Week 1," Monken said Sunday , via Cleveland.com, after Watson played miserably.

That let everyone know that Watson would be the starter. Monken was stuck in a position in which he had to justify the move even though results didn't back it up. It became official Monday, though it's clear the decision was made well before then.

The weird part about it all is Monken told 92.3 The Fan that he had no problem with fans booing Watson, saying, "The business we are in is a performance-based business." Watson has done absolutely nothing, in terms of performance, to get the starting job.

But the Browns have been laying the tracks for this since before last season even ended.

The gaslighting of Browns fans started Dec. 6, when ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Media's Ian Rapoport both reported Watson would be back with the Browns (that was before ESPN and NFL Media merged). The news came absolutely out of nowhere about a player who didn't play last season. It came well before the team hired Monken, as well. Then after that there were glowing reports about Watson. In late April, Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com reported that Watson had emerged as the favorite to start, even though the offseason program really hadn't even begun. There was a long ESPN piece about Watson's redemption that included the premise that he held "no ill will" toward Cleveland, though we found out Saturday he still did. When Watson played decently in the first preseason game, Monken went out of his way to say Watson was "awesome" and "functioned at a high level" even though everyone could see otherwise.

NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

The Browns naming Watson the starter Monday was a decision that seemed to have been made more than nine months ago when they started trying to acclimate Browns fans to the idea Watson would be in their lives another season. That's beyond strange. It's a move with no upside that is agitating a proud and loyal fan base. They floated trial balloons on the move of starting Watson, the fans let the team know they hated the idea, and the Browns went through with it anyway.

It's not that Sanders is a great option, but there's no reason to start Watson. And while teams shouldn't make a decision based on fan reactions, naming a starting quarterback who just waged war with the fan base is stunning. It's an impossibly confounding move by a franchise that won't be good this season but could have at least avoided harassing its supporters.

The factory of sadness has never been sadder.

The Browns naming Watson the starter Monday was a decision that seemed to have been made more than nine months ago when they started trying to acclimate Browns fans to the idea Watson would be in their lives another season. That's beyond strange. It's a move with no upside that is agitating a proud and loyal fan base. They floated trial balloons on the move of starting Watson, the fans let the team know they hated the idea, and the Browns went through with it anyway.

It's not that Sanders is a great option, but there's no reason to start Watson. And while teams shouldn't make a decision based on fan reactions, naming a starting quarterback who just waged war with the fan base is stunning. It's an impossibly confounding move by a franchise that won't be good this season but could have at least avoided harassing its supporters.
The factory of sadness has never been sadder.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson named Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback
articles.summary: Watson won the competition over Shedeur Sanders to be the starter for the Sept. 13 opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the team announced.
articles.body: Deshaun Watson has won the competition to be the Cleveland Browns starting quarterback for the Sept. 13 opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the team announced Monday. Watson, a 10-year veteran, won the competition over Shedeur Sanders as both split reps with the first unit throughout the offseason, training camp and the preseason. The decision will not be popular with Browns fans, who have booed Watson repeatedly during his time in Cleveland. Monken said Sunday that Watson’s comments after the Browns’ 31-7 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Saturday were not expected to be a deciding factor in his final decision. Watson has started only 19 games for Cleveland since being acquired from Houston in 2022 and signing a fully guaranteed, $230 million contract that will likely go down as perhaps one of the worst trades and contracts in NFL history. He is 9-10 with the Browns with 19 touchdown passes, 12 interceptions and an 80.7 passer rating. Many thought Watson’s time with the Browns would be over after he said the boos on Saturday were “personal” and showed “disrespect” after he took the field in Cleveland for the first time in 22 months. “I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in, being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person I know I am, and the character would help, and I guess it hasn’t,” he said after completing 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards and an interception while on the field with players at the bottom of the roster who likely will be cut in a couple of weeks. As Watson was rehabbing from rupturing his right Achilles twice, owner Jimmy Haslam said during last year’s owners meetings that the Browns “took a big swing and miss” when they sent three first-round picks to Houston for Watson in 2022. Watson completed 11 of 15 passes for 126 yards and directed two scoring drives working with other starters and the second team during the first half of the preseason opener at Chicago. Sanders has shown steady improvement throughout the offseason. He started the final seven games of his rookie season, going 3-4 with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Sanders went 9 of 11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and interception during the first half against the Bills. Sanders completed his first eight passes before he was picked off by Damar Hamlin on a pass he threw behind tight end Jermaine Terry. He was 6 of 11 for 79 yards with an interception in the second half against the Bears. Sanders’ biggest improvement is his ability to stand in the pocket as well as move up when he needs to, along with better footwork and decision-making. Even though Sanders will be on the sideline for the opener, he is likely to start at some point this season. In 2022, Watson missed the first 11 games because of a league suspension resulting from his alleged sexual misconduct during massage therapy sessions. He made six starts in 2023 before a season-ending shoulder injury and started seven in 2024 before the first of two Achilles tendon injuries.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Reaction to Deshaun Watson Being Named Browns' QB1 Revealed by Todd Monken
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken addressed his decision Monday to name Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken addressed his decision Monday to name Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders.

Monken said Sanders had an "awesome" reaction to learning he'll be the backup in Week 1.

"You talk about somebody that really understands the long game," the coach told reporters. "That really I think has come to understand the long game. What are we really in this for? What am I in it for? ... Where do we want to be in the long term? He understands that as well as a quarterback."

Monken praised Sanders' work to continue developing ahead of his second season. However, he believes Watson is a better option under center right now, especially since the team starts on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

To some extent, Monken might be taking a longer view of the situation himself.

Any goodwill toward Watson is pretty much gone at this point. The majority of fans will have wanted Sanders to get the keys to the offense.

Now imagine Cleveland getting off to a poor start and Watson delivering more of the same from his first three years with the team — two things that can plausibly happen. The support behind Sanders will be even larger, and he'll get judged even less on the Browns' overall fortunes.

This might be applying too much game theory to Monken's decision. Coaches rarely go into a season trying to lose games, even when their team is rebuilding.

And it doesn't represent a strong endorsement of Sanders that he's not head and shoulders better than a veteran who has been in a years-long decline. Watson's last productive year under center was in 2020.

When Cleveland is widely projected to be one of the NFL's worst teams, why not pin your hopes to the player with far more long-term upside?

Hiring a new coach presents an opportunity for a franchise to wipe the slate clean, and it's way too early to make any concrete judgments about Monken. He probably hasn't made a great first impression on the fans, who are asking whether they'll witness more of the same futility and dysfunction from previous years.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson's 'Poison Pill' in Contract Reported After Winning Browns' QB1 over Shedeur Sanders
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns made the astonishing decision to name Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback on Monday, though releasing him was never really an option.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns made the astonishing decision to name Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback on Monday, though releasing him was never really an option.

As Spotrac noted, doing so would have incurred an $86.2 million dead cap hit for the 2027 season. However, that can be spread between two seasons if he's cut before March 13 in 2027 and designated a post-June 1 release, which would also avoid a $200 million guaranteed salary poison pill:

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

The decision to not only trade for Watson, but also give him a fully-guaranteed contract, remains one of the worst decisions in modern sports history.

Here's what the Browns have gotten for the three first-round picks, one third-rounder, two fourths and the $230 million in fully guaranteed salary over five seasons it took to acquire Watson: 19 total starts, 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions, a 61.2 completion percentage and a 9-10 record.

And after finishing 5-of-12 passes for 35 yards and an interception during Saturday's preseason game, Watson was booed by Cleveland's home crowd and didn't further endear himself to the fan base after the contest.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," he told reporters regarding the boos. "It's a little bit [more] personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing. So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on. ... Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. And that same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt. So what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer?"

It's more complicated than that, of course. Alongside his disappointing performance, Watson's contract has been prohibitive from a team-building standpoint and he also had past scandals that soured him in the eyes of many fans.

He apologized for his remarks on Monday:

It's a virtual guarantee that Watson will not be on the Browns' roster in 2027. He'll leave behind plenty of dead cap space and a strained relationship with Cleveland fans, however.

articles.title: Patriots send WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans for S Jaylen Reed, draft pick
articles.summary: The Texans have found their replacement for injured WR Jayden Higgins.
articles.body:
The Patriots have traded WR Kayshon Boutte to the Houston Texans for safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

The move helps clear up some space in what had become a crowded receiver room in New England , while also giving the Texans some added depth at the position.

Boutte, 24, settled into a solid complementary role over the past two seasons with the Patriots, catching a combined 76 passes for 1,140 yards and 9 TDs in 29 games (23 starts). In last season's playoffs, Boutte led the Patriots with 168 receiving yards in four postseason games.

It's understandable why Boutte would want to go elsewhere this season. With the Patriots signing Romeo Doubs and trading for A.J. Brown , it left Boutte's role in doubt. The Patriots still have Mack Hollins back, and there are two other young receivers on the roster, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams , who could be in line for more snaps and production volume.

There was speculation in June, after the Brown trade was official following months of anticipation, that Boutte could have quietly let New England know that he wouldn't mind playing elsewhere in 2026 .

This is a crucial season for Boutte. The former sixth-round draft pick is entering a contract year, set to hit free agency in the spring, and now appears to have a better chance to increase his market value with a big season in Houston vs. a more crowded New England depth chart.

The move comes on the heels of Texans wide receiver Jayden Higgins tearing his ACL during training camp. He was ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season.

Boutte was used primarily as a perimeter threat in the past two seasons and was effective on vertical shots, but he was also used occasionally in the slot. His production peaked in the first half of last season, before a hamstring injury that reemerged in the postseason, despite some strong playoff moments.

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

The 5-foot-11, 197-pound Boutte projects as a complementary receiver for the Texans alongside Nico Collins , but the progress he's shown the past two seasons suggests there might be some untapped reserves that could elevate his game slightly more.
