articles.title: Deshaun Watson Browns timeline: Inside disastrous trade, contract that brought quarterback to Cleveland
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson's tenure with the Browns has not gone well.
articles.body:
The 2026 Cleveland Browns engaged in the most depressing position battle of the summer to ultimately choose Deshaun Watson . The once-superstar talent has had a rough go of it since joining the franchise in 2022, but will get one more opportunity to prove himself.

There are — thanks to the many things Watson has said and done over the past couple years — legitimate questions about that decision. The Browns seemed to realize as much last year, drafting not one, but two possible quarterbacks of the future in the 2025 NFL Draft. Despite their presence on the roster, Watson won the job yet again.

Given the various ups and downs Watson has experienced across his career, it's worth re-evaluating how the Browns got to this point.

April 27, 2017: Texans select Deshaun Watson in NFL Draft

After a standout college career at Clemson, Watson entered the NFL Draft as one of the top prospects available . While he was the third quarterback taken off the board — Mitchell Trubisky and Patrick Mahomes went higher — Watson didn't have to wait long. The Texans took him with the No. 12 overall pick in the draft, presumably giving the team a quarterback of the future after Brock Osweiler started 14 games for the team the previous season.

Sept. 14, 2017: Deshaun Watson makes his first NFL start

It didn't take long for the Texans to throw Watson into the starting lineup. After the team benched Tom Savage at halftime in Week 1, Watson made his NFL debut, throwing a touchdown and an interception to close out the loss.

The following week, the team decided to stick with Watson under center. He led the team to a 13-9 win in his first-ever start, rushing for a score in the victory.

Nov. 2, 2017: Deshaun Watson tears ACL to end promising rookie season

Watson only made five more starts for the Texans that season. During a November practice, Watson tore his ACL , missing the rest of the season. He finished with 19 passing touchdowns against eight interceptions. Despite only playing in seven games, Watson finished third in the Rookie of the Year voting.

Sept. 5, 2020: Deshaun Watson signs extension with Texans

Watson returned from his ACL injury and blossomed into a superstar with the Texans. Fresh off two straight Pro Bowl seasons, the Texans agreed to pick up Watson's fifth-year option.

But before the start of the 2020 NFL season, the team signed Watson to a four-year, $156 million extension . It solidified his future with the franchise.

Watson responded by going out and throwing for a league-high 4,823 yards and a career-high 33 touchdowns. The Texans, however, went just 4-12.

Jan. 28, 2021: Deshaun Watson demands trade from Texans

Frustration with the state of the team and the front office led to Watson demanding a trade from the Texans. The franchise did not seem interested in honoring that request.

Mar. 17, 2021: Deshaun Watson accused of sexual misconduct

A lawsuit emerged accusing Watson of going "too far" while getting a massage from a female masseuse.

Rumors of the lawsuit came to light a day earlier, leading to Watson issuing a preemptive statement claiming has has "never treated any woman with anything other than the utmost respect."

April 5, 2021: Twenty-two different women join sexual misconduct lawsuit against Deshaun Watson

In less than a month, a number of accusers filed lawsuits against Watson. That number grew to 22 on April 5, leading to the Texans to finally issue a statement .

In the coming days , all but one woman gave up anonymity to proceed with the lawsuits against Watson.

April 19, 2021: Deshaun Watson says all 22 women are lying

Watson's attorney issues a statement claiming all 22 women to file suit against the quarterback are lying .

April 30, 2021: Texans take Davis Mills in 2021 NFL Draft

With both the trade and the off-the-field allegations swirling, the Texans selected Davis Mills in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft. While Mills wasn't a high pick, the selection seemed to hint at the Texans worrying Watson wouldn't be around, either due to a trade or a suspension from the NFL, which had started performing its own investigation.

July 25, 2021: Deshaun Watson reports to Texans training camp

With all those issues still unresolved, Watson reported to training camp in July. The Texans now seemed willing to trade the quarterback, who had not been placed on the NFL's commissioner exempt list yet.

Jan. 9, 2022: Deshaun Watson does not play 2021 season with Texans

The Texans played their final regular-season game Jan. 9, finishing the season 4-13. Despite never being placed on the commissioner's exempt list, Watson didn't play a single down of football for the Texans during the 2021 season.

Mar. 11, 2022: Grand jury declines to indict Deshaun Watson on criminal charges

A Houston grand jury did not find enough evidence to indict Watson of a criminal act . Watson still faced civil lawsuits and the NFL's investigation, but avoiding criminal charges gave the Texans a runway to ship Watson out.

Mar. 18, 2022: Deshaun Watson traded to Browns, signs record contract

Watson waived a no-trade clause to join the Browns. In exchange for Watson, Cleveland gave up three first-round picks, a third-round pick and a fourth-round pick. The team immediately signed Watson to a five-year, fully-guaranteed, $230 million contract . That fully-guaranteed figure remained the most in the NFL until 2025, when Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen exceeded it.

Aug. 18, 2022: NFL suspends Deshaun Watson 11 games, fines him $5 million

After spending the summer settling lawsuits , Watson received an 11-game suspension from the NFL .

That suspension put him out until Week 13, when he would face his former franchise, the Texans, in his first game since the 2021 NFL season.

Dec. 4, 2022: Deshaun Watson makes first Browns start, finishes season

Watson returned from his suspension in time to start against the Texans. In his first Browns' start, Watson threw for just 131 yards and an interception in a 27-14 loss.

He started the team's remaining five games, but looked rusty, finishing the year with seven passing touchdowns against five interceptions.

Nov. 12, 2023: Deshaun Watson out for season with shoulder injury

Watson opened the 2023 NFL season as the Browns' starter and put up middling numbers in his first three games before missing time with a shoulder issue.

After struggling with the injury for a few weeks, Watson was eventually knocked out for the rest of the year during a Week 10 game against the Baltimore Ravens .

He finished the 2023 season with seven passing touchdowns and four interceptions in six games.

Oct. 20, 2024: Deshaun Watson again sustains season-ending injury

Watson again returned to start in 2024, but failed to put up strong numbers in seven starts before rupturing his Achilles against the Cincinnati Bengals . He finished the season with just five passing touchdowns and three interceptions. The Browns were among the worst offenses in the NFL at the time of Watson's injury.

Jan. 10, 2025: Deshaun Watson tears Achilles again

Watson experienced a setback and had to undergo yet another surgery on his Achilles tendon. The issue was expected to keep him out for potentially the entire 2025 NFL season .

Mar. 31, 2025: Browns co-owner Jimmy Haslam says Watson trade was a 'big swing and miss'

The Watson era in Cleveland appeared to be over, as co-owner Jimmy Haslam admitted the trade for the quarterback was a " big swing and miss ."

"We thought we had the quarterback; we didn't. And we gave up a lot of draft picks to get him, so we've got to dig ourselves out of that hole … [The trade] was an entire organization decision and it ends with Dee [Haslam] and I, so hold us accountable."

April 25, 2025: Browns select two quarterbacks in 2025 NFL Draft

Following multiple years of disappointing play and injuries from Watson, the Browns signal they are moving on, taking Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders in the 2025 NFL Draft. Neither are high picks, as Gabriel went in the third round and Sanders was taken in the fifth round .

Those two were expected to compete with veteran Joe Flacco early on.

Dec. 3, 2025: Deshaun Watson cleared to return to practice

Watson made enough progress in his recovery to be cleared to return to practice in December. The move came as Sanders was prepping to make his third NFL start.

Gabriel had started a handful of games with the team as well before an injury pushed him out of the starting role.

Jan. 4, 2026: Browns finish 2025 season 5-12

Though Watson made progress in his recovery, he was never activated from the PUP list and did not appear in a game with the 2025 Browns.

Sanders closed out the season as the team's starter, tossing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in seven starts. It was enough to earn Sanders a Pro Bowl nod after multiple other players opted out of the event.

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

April, 29. 2026: Deshaun Watson starts getting buzz in minicamp

With Watson back, the Browns opted to allow the veteran to compete for the starting job. Positive reports soon emerged, suggesting Watson was performing better than Sanders in minicamp.

Aug. 22, 2026: Deshaun Watson booed by Browns fans in preseason

In what was potentially a deciding game in the Browns' quarterback competition, Watson and Sanders put up middling numbers against the Buffalo Bills in a preseason 31-7 loss.

Watson's performance, however, drew more ire from fans, who booed him when he took the field and then booed him even more after a bad interception. Watson didn't take kindly to that treatment, saying it was personal and " disrespectful. "

Aug. 24, 2026: Deshaun Watson wins Browns' starting job, apologizes to fans

It's 2026 and, somehow, Watson has returned. The Browns officially named him the team's starter over Sanders on Monday.

The 2026 season will mark the final year of Watson's $230 million fully guaranteed contract. Heading into 2026, here's how he's performed with the Browns since the trade:

In Watson's first public appearance since that news, he apologized for the way he handled Saturday's game, saying his emotions got the best of him.

Watson, who hasn't thrown a pass in an NFL game since 2024, will open the year under center when the Browns travel to play the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1. The Browns will also play their Week 2 game on the road before Watson returns to Cleveland to take on the Carolina Panthers at home in Week 3.

Barring a fantastic start to the season, Watson may not receive the warmest response from Browns fans when — or if — he takes the field for that game.

The following week, the team decided to stick with Watson under center. He led the team to a 13-9 win in his first-ever start, rushing for a score in the victory.
Nov. 2, 2017: Deshaun Watson tears ACL to end promising rookie season

Watson only made five more starts for the Texans that season. During a November practice, Watson tore his ACL , missing the rest of the season. He finished with 19 passing touchdowns against eight interceptions. Despite only playing in seven games, Watson finished third in the Rookie of the Year voting.
Sept. 5, 2020: Deshaun Watson signs extension with Texans
Watson returned from his ACL injury and blossomed into a superstar with the Texans. Fresh off two straight Pro Bowl seasons, the Texans agreed to pick up Watson's fifth-year option.
But before the start of the 2020 NFL season, the team signed Watson to a four-year, $156 million extension . It solidified his future with the franchise.
Watson responded by going out and throwing for a league-high 4,823 yards and a career-high 33 touchdowns. The Texans, however, went just 4-12.
Jan. 28, 2021: Deshaun Watson demands trade from Texans
Frustration with the state of the team and the front office led to Watson demanding a trade from the Texans. The franchise did not seem interested in honoring that request.
Mar. 17, 2021: Deshaun Watson accused of sexual misconduct
A lawsuit emerged accusing Watson of going "too far" while getting a massage from a female masseuse.
Rumors of the lawsuit came to light a day earlier, leading to Watson issuing a preemptive statement claiming has has "never treated any woman with anything other than the utmost respect."
April 5, 2021: Twenty-two different women join sexual misconduct lawsuit against Deshaun Watson
In less than a month, a number of accusers filed lawsuits against Watson. That number grew to 22 on April 5, leading to the Texans to finally issue a statement .
In the coming days , all but one woman gave up anonymity to proceed with the lawsuits against Watson.
April 19, 2021: Deshaun Watson says all 22 women are lying
Watson's attorney issues a statement claiming all 22 women to file suit against the quarterback are lying .
April 30, 2021: Texans take Davis Mills in 2021 NFL Draft

With both the trade and the off-the-field allegations swirling, the Texans selected Davis Mills in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft. While Mills wasn't a high pick, the selection seemed to hint at the Texans worrying Watson wouldn't be around, either due to a trade or a suspension from the NFL, which had started performing its own investigation.
July 25, 2021: Deshaun Watson reports to Texans training camp

With all those issues still unresolved, Watson reported to training camp in July. The Texans now seemed willing to trade the quarterback, who had not been placed on the NFL's commissioner exempt list yet.
Jan. 9, 2022: Deshaun Watson does not play 2021 season with Texans

The Texans played their final regular-season game Jan. 9, finishing the season 4-13. Despite never being placed on the commissioner's exempt list, Watson didn't play a single down of football for the Texans during the 2021 season.
Mar. 11, 2022: Grand jury declines to indict Deshaun Watson on criminal charges

A Houston grand jury did not find enough evidence to indict Watson of a criminal act . Watson still faced civil lawsuits and the NFL's investigation, but avoiding criminal charges gave the Texans a runway to ship Watson out.
Mar. 18, 2022: Deshaun Watson traded to Browns, signs record contract

Watson waived a no-trade clause to join the Browns. In exchange for Watson, Cleveland gave up three first-round picks, a third-round pick and a fourth-round pick. The team immediately signed Watson to a five-year, fully-guaranteed, $230 million contract . That fully-guaranteed figure remained the most in the NFL until 2025, when Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen exceeded it.
Aug. 18, 2022: NFL suspends Deshaun Watson 11 games, fines him $5 million
After spending the summer settling lawsuits , Watson received an 11-game suspension from the NFL .
That suspension put him out until Week 13, when he would face his former franchise, the Texans, in his first game since the 2021 NFL season.
Dec. 4, 2022: Deshaun Watson makes first Browns start, finishes season
Watson returned from his suspension in time to start against the Texans. In his first Browns' start, Watson threw for just 131 yards and an interception in a 27-14 loss.
He started the team's remaining five games, but looked rusty, finishing the year with seven passing touchdowns against five interceptions.
Nov. 12, 2023: Deshaun Watson out for season with shoulder injury
Watson opened the 2023 NFL season as the Browns' starter and put up middling numbers in his first three games before missing time with a shoulder issue.
After struggling with the injury for a few weeks, Watson was eventually knocked out for the rest of the year during a Week 10 game against the Baltimore Ravens .
He finished the 2023 season with seven passing touchdowns and four interceptions in six games.
Oct. 20, 2024: Deshaun Watson again sustains season-ending injury

Watson again returned to start in 2024, but failed to put up strong numbers in seven starts before rupturing his Achilles against the Cincinnati Bengals . He finished the season with just five passing touchdowns and three interceptions. The Browns were among the worst offenses in the NFL at the time of Watson's injury.
Jan. 10, 2025: Deshaun Watson tears Achilles again
Watson experienced a setback and had to undergo yet another surgery on his Achilles tendon. The issue was expected to keep him out for potentially the entire 2025 NFL season .
Mar. 31, 2025: Browns co-owner Jimmy Haslam says Watson trade was a 'big swing and miss'
The Watson era in Cleveland appeared to be over, as co-owner Jimmy Haslam admitted the trade for the quarterback was a " big swing and miss ."

"We thought we had the quarterback; we didn't. And we gave up a lot of draft picks to get him, so we've got to dig ourselves out of that hole … [The trade] was an entire organization decision and it ends with Dee [Haslam] and I, so hold us accountable."
April 25, 2025: Browns select two quarterbacks in 2025 NFL Draft

Following multiple years of disappointing play and injuries from Watson, the Browns signal they are moving on, taking Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders in the 2025 NFL Draft. Neither are high picks, as Gabriel went in the third round and Sanders was taken in the fifth round .
Those two were expected to compete with veteran Joe Flacco early on.
Dec. 3, 2025: Deshaun Watson cleared to return to practice
Watson made enough progress in his recovery to be cleared to return to practice in December. The move came as Sanders was prepping to make his third NFL start.
Gabriel had started a handful of games with the team as well before an injury pushed him out of the starting role.
Jan. 4, 2026: Browns finish 2025 season 5-12
Though Watson made progress in his recovery, he was never activated from the PUP list and did not appear in a game with the 2025 Browns.

Sanders closed out the season as the team's starter, tossing seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in seven starts. It was enough to earn Sanders a Pro Bowl nod after multiple other players opted out of the event.
NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders
Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'
49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest
April, 29. 2026: Deshaun Watson starts getting buzz in minicamp
With Watson back, the Browns opted to allow the veteran to compete for the starting job. Positive reports soon emerged, suggesting Watson was performing better than Sanders in minicamp.
Aug. 22, 2026: Deshaun Watson booed by Browns fans in preseason
In what was potentially a deciding game in the Browns' quarterback competition, Watson and Sanders put up middling numbers against the Buffalo Bills in a preseason 31-7 loss.

Watson's performance, however, drew more ire from fans, who booed him when he took the field and then booed him even more after a bad interception. Watson didn't take kindly to that treatment, saying it was personal and " disrespectful. "
Aug. 24, 2026: Deshaun Watson wins Browns' starting job, apologizes to fans
It's 2026 and, somehow, Watson has returned. The Browns officially named him the team's starter over Sanders on Monday.
The 2026 season will mark the final year of Watson's $230 million fully guaranteed contract. Heading into 2026, here's how he's performed with the Browns since the trade:
In Watson's first public appearance since that news, he apologized for the way he handled Saturday's game, saying his emotions got the best of him.

Watson, who hasn't thrown a pass in an NFL game since 2024, will open the year under center when the Browns travel to play the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1. The Browns will also play their Week 2 game on the road before Watson returns to Cleveland to take on the Carolina Panthers at home in Week 3.
Barring a fantastic start to the season, Watson may not receive the warmest response from Browns fans when — or if — he takes the field for that game.

articles.title: Updated Patriots, Texans WR Depth Charts After Kayshon Boutte Trade amid Fantasy Football Drafts
articles.summary: With Jayden Higgins out for the season because of a torn ACL, the Houston Texans reportedly continued bolstering their wide receiver depth Monday.
articles.body:
With Jayden Higgins out for the season because of a torn ACL , the Houston Texans reportedly continued bolstering their wide receiver depth Monday.

Tom Pelissero of the Ringer reported the Texans sent safety Jaylen Reed and a draft pick to the New England Patriots in exchange for Kayshon Boutte. This comes after Houston added both Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones.

Here is a look at the wide receiver depth charts for both teams after the move:

Fantasy Football Sleepers Getting Buzz 🐝

LWR: Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Jared Wayne, Zay Jones

RWR: Kayshon Boutte, Tank Dell, Justin Watson

SWR: Jaylin Noel, Lewis Bond, Sterling Shepard

LWR: A.J. Brown, Kyle Williams, Cameron Dorner

RWR: Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins, Kyle Dixon

SWR: DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, Nick DeGennaro

The trade bolsters Houston's overall ceiling in its race for an AFC South title and from a fantasy perspective.

After all, there were plenty of question marks about the room following Higgins' injury. Tank Dell hasn't played since the 2024 campaign, and Nico Collins was the only wide receiver on the team last season to finish with more than 525 receiving yards.

In fact, Higgins was second in that category, which meant it remained very much up in the air who would be the No. 2 option outside of Collins.

Enter Boutte, who had a career-high six touchdown catches last season and a combined 1,149 receiving yards the last two years. While he isn't someone who is realistically going to challenge for 1,000-plus yards in 2026, he is a proven option who should be able to fully capitalize on the double teams that Collins will surely draw.

That also makes him more valuable from a fantasy perspective than he would have been in New England this season after the reigning AFC champions added both A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs to the room.

Boutte likely would have been the third option at best, and that's not even including tight end Hunter Henry.

That Boutte was moved does not come as a surprise, as Karen Guregian of Mass Live reported he "requested a trade as far back as April." What's more, ESPN's Mike Reiss reported earlier this month he "would welcome a trade if the right situation presented itself."

It did present itself, and Boutte appears ready to take over the No. 2 role in Houston's offense alongside Collins. That also gives Dell a bit more time to work his way back into form after being away so long.

If everything goes according to plan, C.J. Stroud could have three game-changing wide receivers to work with this season following this trade.

articles.title: Malik Nabers' Injury Status Updated by Giants' John Harbaugh Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Malik Nabers is in the midst of an important week in his recovery from the torn ACL he suffered during the 2025 campaign.
articles.body:
Malik Nabers is in the midst of an important week in his recovery from the torn ACL he suffered during the 2025 campaign.

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters Sunday the wide receiver could shed his no-contact jersey he's been practicing with as soon as this week.

"That's a possibility," Harbaugh said. "We'll just have to see where he's at."

He then provided another update Monday and said "it's reasonable to assume" Nabers could take the field in Week 1:

While the Giants don't take the field for the regular season until Sept. 13 when they face the rival Dallas Cowboys, they surely want their star receiver to have some practice time without the no-contact jersey before Week 1.

Nabers himself wouldn't commit to playing in Week 1 when he discussed how difficult the recovery process has been and instead took a long-term approach with his health:

"The most important thing is my health," Nabers said Monday. "The most important thing is just completing every milestone that they have in front of me, giving good effort, continuing to come out here and be a great teammate to my teammates."

At just 23 years old, a long-term approach is the correct one.

The Giants may be a year or two away from being legitimate contenders in the NFC East, and Nabers figures to be a major part of it as one of the best young receivers in the league. He posted 109 catches for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a Pro Bowler in his rookie season in 2024 and was primed to build on that in his second season.

However, the torn ACL limited him to just four games in 2025 and has kept his health under the spotlight heading into the 2026 campaign.

Shedding the no-contact jersey is a key step back to make sure he can deal with tackles in the open field, and it seems like he is one step closer to a full comeback.

articles.title: New Aaron Donald Rumors on Contract Being Hold Up for Rams Return, DT Won't 'Play for Free'
articles.summary: Speculation about whether Aaron Donald will come back for the Los Angeles Rams has continued throughout the summer, and there still isn't a resolution.
articles.body:
Speculation about whether Aaron Donald will come back for the Los Angeles Rams has continued throughout the summer, and there still isn't a resolution.

During a Monday an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show (35-second mark), Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported the money aspect of the situation could be playing a role.

"This isn't from Rams people or from Donald's people, but one thing that has continually come up when I talk to other people in the league about it is, 'how do you work out the money part of it? How much are you paying him? How does it fit into their budget, both cash and cap?' So there's that piece of it too. I don't think he's going to want to come out there and play for free."

Still, the Rams have surely thought about the money part since speculation began that Donald would be coming back shortly after they traded for Myles Garrett.

With that as the backdrop, Breer suggested the financial component isn't the most important one.

"I think the bigger piece, and this is just me talking, is him feeling comfortable that he can go out there and be Aaron Donald," he said.. "… The trouble with that is it's not just his ability to play football at a high level. It's to be Aaron Donald."

Playing like peak Aaron Donald is a significant amount to ask of any player in NFL history.

The future Hall of Famer is 35 years old and hasn't played an NFL game since the 2023 campaign. He may remain dominant, especially playing alongside Garrett, but expecting him to be the same version of himself who put together a legendary resume is a bit unrealistic.

After all, that resume includes a Super Bowl title, three Defensive Player of the Year awards, a Defensive Rookie of the Year, eight First-Team All-Pro nods and 10 Pro Bowl selections. He led the NFL with 20.5 sacks in 2018 and has 111 for his career.

Breer reported the Rams will have a plan for him if and when he does return that will include a limited snap count to maximize his effectiveness.

Even if he isn't quite as effective as he was when he was arguably the best player in the league, he will surely be a difference-maker for the defense. First, though, he has to officially decide whether he will come back in 2026.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson beating Shedeur Sanders as Browns' Week 1 starter is just the beginning. Now, a tenuous reality awaits
articles.summary: Multiple sources with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors suggest: The decision to name Watson rather than Sanders did not arrive via a landslid...
articles.body:
When Deshaun Watson booed the boos that rained down from fans on Saturday , the Cleveland Browns quarterback questioned not only his fan base's actions but also their intentions.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson told reporters after the 31-7 loss.

The line left plenty to unpack about the history between quarterback and fan base. It also seemed to gain further relevance Monday when the Browns named Watson their starting quarterback for their season opener. Because while Watson (accurately or not) believed fans' boos had "nothing to do with the performance," Cleveland's decision to name Watson its Week 1 starter has plenty to do with it. If the Browns' decision was about fan popularity or podium performance or medium- to long-term upside, 2025 fifth-round pick Shedeur Sanders would have received the nod Monday.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

Instead, a conversation about who gives the club its best chance to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in Jacksonville on Sept. 13 unfolded.

"You don't ignore the fans and the tax that maybe something like that can put on the organization, but we also have to make football decisions," a person with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors told Yahoo Sports. "You also can't be emotionally hijacked and not make what you think is the sound, right football decision."

Multiple sources with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors suggest: The decision to name Watson rather than Sanders did not arrive via a landslide. This was not a decision about who is "good" or "bad" and perhaps not a decision about who is the better or worse NFL quarterback.

"I do think there's maybe a little bit of an element here in terms of what you value in terms of their relative strengths and weaknesses," a second person with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors told Yahoo Sports. "Deshaun's athletic. You'll have the operation right. He's really good pre-snap. Shedeur, he's accurate. He's very, very poised in the pocket. He's a good drop-back passer and he can create enough off schedule with his legs, but you're not going to do QB designed run."

Monken opted to promote the player with 72 career starts whom he believes is superior in nuances like the silent count required on the road, rather than the seven-start player whose quarterbacking skills may deserve the edge.

Watson's strengths — which are different from those of Sanders, whether or not they are better — won out.

That tenuous reality was clear even as Monken sandwiched a "this is not a week-to-week decision" comment between his notes that Watson is going to start "against Jacksonville" and "ultimately, we're about Week 1."

How much cushion does Watson have and what would prompt consideration for an eventual change?

Those are questions the Browns must ask themselves even before their season officially starts.

Monken made clear on Sunday that he understands what's expected as he fielded questions about Watson's emotional outburst.

"The business we're in is a performance-based business," Monken told reporters. "It is what it is. When we expect a service, we're going to be disappointed when we don't get that service. If you go to a restaurant and your soup comes out cold, you're going to be upset. If you order from the grocery store and six of your eggs are broken, you're going to be pissed. So, I get it, that's what we're in. That's why we're paid what we are, to perform at a high level, and when we don't, there are repercussions. We've run to this smoke.

"This is the job we've chosen, so this is part of it."

After rocky weekend, what does Watson's starting role mean?

For a stretch over the weekend, there was reason to wonder if Watson had forfeited the starting right that his offseason and training camp performance had narrowly earned him.

Insulting a fan base is rarely a winning strategy in professional sports. Insulting a fan base as a player years removed from strong performances and winning is still dicier. Watson's apology on Monday , after he was named the Browns' Week 1 starter, might resonate with some. His background facing allegations of sexual assault and misconduct, and the multiple injuries he's suffered while costing three first-round draft picks in a 2022 trade and a $230 million fully guaranteed contract, make him generally unsympathetic to others.

But Watson's Monday opening statement struck a different tone than he's had since arriving in Cleveland.

"My emotions got the best of me," Watson admitted of his Saturday comments in which he called Browns fans booing a "disrespectful" gesture. "I'm human. I take full responsibility of that. Moving forward, I want to make sure I put the best product out there for the team."

He noted also that "I understand the frustration" from fans watching a losing product and believes winning will help him "earn the respect and loyalty of the rest of the fan base."

#Browns Deshaun Watson apologizes for his postgame remarks, saying he’s human. Wants to win for the fans: pic.twitter.com/LXbIvkPgdO — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) August 24, 2026

#Browns Deshaun Watson apologizes for his postgame remarks, saying he’s human. Wants to win for the fans: pic.twitter.com/LXbIvkPgdO

Watson's actions must echo and then speak louder than his words in the coming weeks. But in the short term, perhaps they send a message to Cleveland's locker room that the club's quarterback realizes his comments were a mistake.

Perhaps that was the point, if not the best possible outcome of Watson's mea culpa. Did a large subsection of fans shift their core beliefs because their quarterback made a 2 1/2-minute statement? Unlikely. But did a locker room and coaching staff far higher on Watson than their fan base perhaps receive some reassurance that his lost-cool comments won't become a norm? That's more plausible.

Earning back some grace from colleagues after this weekend would be wise. Because not only did Sanders rise above the news conference drama Watson created, but Sanders also played better than Watson in the last benchmark of the decision that ultimately wasn't close enough to close the gap in the competition. Evaluators say snaps with each phase of the roster matter. But when trying to predict Week 1 performance, each quarterback's snaps with the starters ultimately prove most representative.

Thus Watson's preseason Week 1 stat line of 11-of-15 passing for 126 yards and a lost fumble ultimately became a part of his win relative to Sanders' Week 2 showing of 9-for-11 passing for 74 yards, a touchdown and an interception (plenty of caveats exist for each performance amid a preseason atmosphere and in-flux roster).

Watson's early Cleveland games paled in comparison to his Houston Texans tenure, as his completion percentage dropped from 67.8% in Houston to 61.2% in 19 Cleveland games across three years. His production went from 269.2 passing yards per game in Houston to 177.1. Add in Achilles tears that will separate his last start and his next by 693 days, and questions abound.

But Watson is optimistic that teaming up with Monken will unlock some of his strengths that haven't flashed recently.

"We haven't showcased my full talent and ability to run in this offense, being able to run and being able to use my athletic ability, getting outside the pocket, being able to do some other QB-driven stuff," Watson said. "So, I'm excited to see what we can cook up getting ready for Week 1."

Why Watson's starting nod doesn't spell Sanders' end with Browns

Browns decision-makers stressed on Monday: Giving Watson the early nod does not mean they've given up on Sanders.

No one's saying publicly or directly that Sanders is likely to start later in the year. But consider Cleveland's history of quarterback carousels and its two first-round picks looming in 2027: If Sanders is healthy all year, it will be a surprise if he doesn't receive a start.

"Shedeur has improved a ton," the first source with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making process said, echoing Monken's public sentiments. "You can argue where he's coming from, fine, but he's improved a lot. And he still could not be the better one. Or could not be the one that's right. I don't know why both can't be true.

"Because the other guy is more ready or is the right choice, in our minds, doesn't mean Shedeur sucks. Both things can be true. It could just be, 'Hey, this is the right decision for us right now.'"

Watson's performance Week 1 at Jacksonville and Week 2 at Tampa Bay — against his predecessor in former Browns' first overall pick Baker Mayfield , no less — will dictate what's the right decision for the Browns afterward.

Yes, Cleveland opening at home Week 3 amid their famously unsupportive-of-Watson crowd will factor into a decision. Maybe early wins will win Watson some favor with the fans. Maybe the need to build a young roster will become more pressing. Could Sanders end up starting Week 3 through the rest of the season and demonstrate how much he's advanced from a year ago? That's plausible. If that happens, will the Browns regret not rolling with him Week 1?

"It's not actually that simple with the variables," Monken said in explaining the quarterback decision to Yahoo Sports on Aug. 7. "A number of players, when it's that close, you don't know for sure. You think you know. But you know what? At some point, you put Lamar Jackson in the first time. They didn't know, and at first, they probably thought he couldn't do what he's done.

"And then he developed at it, and he got better."

The Browns will need to decide what factors will most dictate their roster battles as the season progresses. How will Monken and Co. react if the team is 2-0 but their offense is ineffective, or if they are 0-2 but Watson has played well? How about if the Browns return home at 1-1, with an average Watson and an average offense — but also a young talent in Sanders whom at least some in the building believe could approach quality starter level?

Why Sean Payton ordered a life-sized cardboard cutout of OC Davis Webb to Broncos camp

After chippy Broncos practice sends Bo Nix to ground, Denver reminds defense its goal is to be 'smart bullies'

From Fred Warner cautioning Cam Ward to De'Zhaun Stribling unsatisfied, 5 takeaways from San Francisco 49ers camp

At some point, the medium- to long-term future of the position will creep into decisions about the short-term future. And there's a reality in which this gives Sanders his best chance of the season.

Because unlike Watson, starting Week 1 on the road with multiple receivers who haven't played an NFL game and a play-caller in Monken still adapting to his personnel, the insertion of Sanders later in the season could position him to enter an offense that has more intel on what it needs most and how it can best succeed.

The Browns expect Sanders to stay engaged until that moment arrives, the younger quarterback aware that his next start in Cleveland is a matter of when not if under a staff that sees his potential even if noting it's rawer than that of Watson.

"Ultimately, we felt over the course of training camp and the offseason that [Watson] was ahead of Shedeur," Monken told reporters on Monday. "Shedeur has closed that gap, for sure, and that's a credit to him. …

"We met this morning for a good long time, and all he had was a smile on his face, because he understands what's really in front of him: not really a short-term, more of a long-term decision.

"This is a player who's going to work his butt off to get better, and he already has."
paragraphs: When Deshaun Watson booed the boos that rained down from fans on Saturday , the Cleveland Browns quarterback questioned not only his fan base's actions but also their intentions.
"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson told reporters after the 31-7 loss.

The line left plenty to unpack about the history between quarterback and fan base. It also seemed to gain further relevance Monday when the Browns named Watson their starting quarterback for their season opener. Because while Watson (accurately or not) believed fans' boos had "nothing to do with the performance," Cleveland's decision to name Watson its Week 1 starter has plenty to do with it. If the Browns' decision was about fan popularity or podium performance or medium- to long-term upside, 2025 fifth-round pick Shedeur Sanders would have received the nod Monday.
Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!
Instead, a conversation about who gives the club its best chance to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in Jacksonville on Sept. 13 unfolded.

"You don't ignore the fans and the tax that maybe something like that can put on the organization, but we also have to make football decisions," a person with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors told Yahoo Sports. "You also can't be emotionally hijacked and not make what you think is the sound, right football decision."

Multiple sources with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors suggest: The decision to name Watson rather than Sanders did not arrive via a landslide. This was not a decision about who is "good" or "bad" and perhaps not a decision about who is the better or worse NFL quarterback.

"I do think there's maybe a little bit of an element here in terms of what you value in terms of their relative strengths and weaknesses," a second person with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making factors told Yahoo Sports. "Deshaun's athletic. You'll have the operation right. He's really good pre-snap. Shedeur, he's accurate. He's very, very poised in the pocket. He's a good drop-back passer and he can create enough off schedule with his legs, but you're not going to do QB designed run."

Monken opted to promote the player with 72 career starts whom he believes is superior in nuances like the silent count required on the road, rather than the seven-start player whose quarterbacking skills may deserve the edge.
Watson's strengths — which are different from those of Sanders, whether or not they are better — won out.

That tenuous reality was clear even as Monken sandwiched a "this is not a week-to-week decision" comment between his notes that Watson is going to start "against Jacksonville" and "ultimately, we're about Week 1."
How much cushion does Watson have and what would prompt consideration for an eventual change?
Those are questions the Browns must ask themselves even before their season officially starts.
Monken made clear on Sunday that he understands what's expected as he fielded questions about Watson's emotional outburst.

"The business we're in is a performance-based business," Monken told reporters. "It is what it is. When we expect a service, we're going to be disappointed when we don't get that service. If you go to a restaurant and your soup comes out cold, you're going to be upset. If you order from the grocery store and six of your eggs are broken, you're going to be pissed. So, I get it, that's what we're in. That's why we're paid what we are, to perform at a high level, and when we don't, there are repercussions. We've run to this smoke.
"This is the job we've chosen, so this is part of it."
After rocky weekend, what does Watson's starting role mean?
For a stretch over the weekend, there was reason to wonder if Watson had forfeited the starting right that his offseason and training camp performance had narrowly earned him.

Insulting a fan base is rarely a winning strategy in professional sports. Insulting a fan base as a player years removed from strong performances and winning is still dicier. Watson's apology on Monday , after he was named the Browns' Week 1 starter, might resonate with some. His background facing allegations of sexual assault and misconduct, and the multiple injuries he's suffered while costing three first-round draft picks in a 2022 trade and a $230 million fully guaranteed contract, make him generally unsympathetic to others.
But Watson's Monday opening statement struck a different tone than he's had since arriving in Cleveland.

"My emotions got the best of me," Watson admitted of his Saturday comments in which he called Browns fans booing a "disrespectful" gesture. "I'm human. I take full responsibility of that. Moving forward, I want to make sure I put the best product out there for the team."
He noted also that "I understand the frustration" from fans watching a losing product and believes winning will help him "earn the respect and loyalty of the rest of the fan base."
#Browns Deshaun Watson apologizes for his postgame remarks, saying he’s human. Wants to win for the fans: pic.twitter.com/LXbIvkPgdO — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) August 24, 2026
#Browns Deshaun Watson apologizes for his postgame remarks, saying he’s human. Wants to win for the fans: pic.twitter.com/LXbIvkPgdO

Watson's actions must echo and then speak louder than his words in the coming weeks. But in the short term, perhaps they send a message to Cleveland's locker room that the club's quarterback realizes his comments were a mistake.

Perhaps that was the point, if not the best possible outcome of Watson's mea culpa. Did a large subsection of fans shift their core beliefs because their quarterback made a 2 1/2-minute statement? Unlikely. But did a locker room and coaching staff far higher on Watson than their fan base perhaps receive some reassurance that his lost-cool comments won't become a norm? That's more plausible.

Earning back some grace from colleagues after this weekend would be wise. Because not only did Sanders rise above the news conference drama Watson created, but Sanders also played better than Watson in the last benchmark of the decision that ultimately wasn't close enough to close the gap in the competition. Evaluators say snaps with each phase of the roster matter. But when trying to predict Week 1 performance, each quarterback's snaps with the starters ultimately prove most representative.

Thus Watson's preseason Week 1 stat line of 11-of-15 passing for 126 yards and a lost fumble ultimately became a part of his win relative to Sanders' Week 2 showing of 9-for-11 passing for 74 yards, a touchdown and an interception (plenty of caveats exist for each performance amid a preseason atmosphere and in-flux roster).

Watson's early Cleveland games paled in comparison to his Houston Texans tenure, as his completion percentage dropped from 67.8% in Houston to 61.2% in 19 Cleveland games across three years. His production went from 269.2 passing yards per game in Houston to 177.1. Add in Achilles tears that will separate his last start and his next by 693 days, and questions abound.
But Watson is optimistic that teaming up with Monken will unlock some of his strengths that haven't flashed recently.

"We haven't showcased my full talent and ability to run in this offense, being able to run and being able to use my athletic ability, getting outside the pocket, being able to do some other QB-driven stuff," Watson said. "So, I'm excited to see what we can cook up getting ready for Week 1."
Why Watson's starting nod doesn't spell Sanders' end with Browns
Browns decision-makers stressed on Monday: Giving Watson the early nod does not mean they've given up on Sanders.

No one's saying publicly or directly that Sanders is likely to start later in the year. But consider Cleveland's history of quarterback carousels and its two first-round picks looming in 2027: If Sanders is healthy all year, it will be a surprise if he doesn't receive a start.

"Shedeur has improved a ton," the first source with knowledge of the Browns' decision-making process said, echoing Monken's public sentiments. "You can argue where he's coming from, fine, but he's improved a lot. And he still could not be the better one. Or could not be the one that's right. I don't know why both can't be true.
"Because the other guy is more ready or is the right choice, in our minds, doesn't mean Shedeur sucks. Both things can be true. It could just be, 'Hey, this is the right decision for us right now.'"

Watson's performance Week 1 at Jacksonville and Week 2 at Tampa Bay — against his predecessor in former Browns' first overall pick Baker Mayfield , no less — will dictate what's the right decision for the Browns afterward.

Yes, Cleveland opening at home Week 3 amid their famously unsupportive-of-Watson crowd will factor into a decision. Maybe early wins will win Watson some favor with the fans. Maybe the need to build a young roster will become more pressing. Could Sanders end up starting Week 3 through the rest of the season and demonstrate how much he's advanced from a year ago? That's plausible. If that happens, will the Browns regret not rolling with him Week 1?

"It's not actually that simple with the variables," Monken said in explaining the quarterback decision to Yahoo Sports on Aug. 7. "A number of players, when it's that close, you don't know for sure. You think you know. But you know what? At some point, you put Lamar Jackson in the first time. They didn't know, and at first, they probably thought he couldn't do what he's done.
"And then he developed at it, and he got better."

The Browns will need to decide what factors will most dictate their roster battles as the season progresses. How will Monken and Co. react if the team is 2-0 but their offense is ineffective, or if they are 0-2 but Watson has played well? How about if the Browns return home at 1-1, with an average Watson and an average offense — but also a young talent in Sanders whom at least some in the building believe could approach quality starter level?

"Ultimately, we felt over the course of training camp and the offseason that [Watson] was ahead of Shedeur," Monken told reporters on Monday. "Shedeur has closed that gap, for sure, and that's a credit to him. …
"We met this morning for a good long time, and all he had was a smile on his face, because he understands what's really in front of him: not really a short-term, more of a long-term decision.

articles.title: NFL: At least one in four dead players had brain disease, says study
articles.summary: A new study says at least one in four ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had a degenerative brain disease but the true figure could be much higher.
articles.body:
As many as 97.7% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 could have had brain disease related to repeated blows to the head, a new study says.

Researchers looked at 878 former players who died during that period, with 235 having donated their brains to research.

Of those, 215 were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease which can only be diagnosed after death.

The study, published in the British Medical Journal , external , also found dementia was common among brain donors.

"We and others have shown that in NFL players, specifically, there is about a four times higher rate of death from neurodegenerative disease than the general population," said the report's lead author Daniel Daneshvar, an associate professor at Harvard Medical School.

"These findings indicate that NFL players have a higher prevalence of CTE at death than has been previously shown in multiple community based studies."

Researchers calculated a "conservative minimum" of CTE prevalence among those who died in the six-year period to be 24.5% - rising to a "maximum" 97.7%.

They have urged the NFL to take prevention measures to reduce repetitive head impacts across all levels of the sport.

Dallas Cowboys player who died by suicide diagnosed with brain disease Published 8 July

Dallas Cowboys player who died by suicide diagnosed with brain disease

NFL admits football-brain disease link Published 15 March 2016

New research finds link between head impacts & CTE Published 27 July 2022

New research finds link between head impacts & CTE

"The bulk of the head impacts that these former NFL players experienced didn't occur at the NFL level," Danshvar said.

"They occurred at the collegiate level and at the high school level and in many cases the youth level. And all of those cumulative hits to the head added up to result in an increased risk."

An NFL spokesperson said: "The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts.

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust - and expanding - set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well being.

"We encourage former players to utilise these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

CTE among American football players has been a growing issue in recent years. A 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement for the NFL limited the number of contact practices.

Following a long-running class action, in 2016 the NFL agreed a $1bn (Â£700m) settlement with more than 5,000 former players.

articles.title: Why did the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal fade so quickly? NFL analyst questions the silence
articles.summary: NFL News: The Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel controversy made waves in April 2026 and then, almost without warning, stopped. Photographs reportedly showing the .
articles.body: The Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel controversy made waves in April 2026 and then, almost without warning, stopped. Photographs reportedly showing the former Athletic reporter and New England Patriots head coach together at a Sedona resort surfaced, Russini resigned following an internal review, and the NFL media largely moved on. Analyst Drew Boylhart does not think that silence was accidental. He believes the story was inconvenient for too many powerful people inside the league, and that is exactly why it disappeared.Why did the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel scandal receive so little media coverage?Boylhart made his position clear on X, arguing that the NFL and its media partners had every reason to keep the story contained. "Notice how the NFL, with help from the media, has buried the Dianna Russini/Mike Vrabel scandal," he wrote. "Why, you ask? Because she knows all the players, owners, and coaches who are doing the same thing. WOKE Goodell doesn't want to open that Pandora's box."His argument is speculative, not evidential. But the underlying concern he raises is worth examining. Russini was not a fringe figure. She was a prominent NFL insider with access to coaches, front offices, and locker rooms. She voted in the Associated Press balloting for major awards including MVP and Coach of the Year. The ethical questions her situation raised about journalism, access, and proximity to power were real, regardless of what specifically happened between her and Vrabel.The Athletic did conduct an internal review. Russini resigned. The review was still ongoing at the time the story faded. Vrabel, after a brief absence, remained in his role with the Patriots. For something that touched on media ethics, journalistic integrity, and league accountability, the conversation moved on remarkably fast.Boylhart's read is that one high-profile investigation risked pulling back a curtain the league preferred to keep closed.What did Aaron Rodgers say about the NFL silence on the Dianna Russini scandal?Aaron Rodgers was one of the few prominent voices in the league who pushed back on the quiet. Appearing on The Pat McAfee Show, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback was openly frustrated. "You have literally an individual that maybe used to work at ESPN that covers our league at the highest level, and there's a major scandal, and it's just like nobody can [Explicit] talk about it. What are we even doing here?" he said.Rodgers did not provide any new information. What he did was name the discomfort a lot of people seemed to be feeling but were not willing to say out loud. When an NFL quarterback is the loudest voice questioning media accountability, that says something about how thoroughly the story was avoided by those with more to lose.Whether Boylhart's specific theory holds weight or not, the broader pattern he points to is harder to dismiss. Russini's departure resolved the immediate situation. The questions it raised about access journalism in the NFL did not go away just because the news cycle moved on.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Updated Rankings and Advice for Team Names
articles.summary: Opening kick of the 2026 NFL season is barely two weeks away.
articles.body:
Opening kick of the 2026 NFL season is barely two weeks away.

For fantasy football managers who haven't finalized their draft plans, what's the hold-up?

Well, maybe you're trying to extract as much information as possible before building that blueprint. So, you need to stay up-to-date on things like updated rankings and movement among fantasy stocks from two weeks of preseason action.

We're here to provide both, plus some bonus tips on how to craft the best team name.

Stock up: Jonathon Brooks, RB, Carolina Panthers

Stalled to this point by two ACL tears, Brooks might finally be healthy enough to make his mark. The 2024 second-round pick seized his opportunity Friday night with Carolina's starting group, tallying five carries for 18 yards and a score.

Meanwhile, his primary competitor for carries, Chuba Hubbard, was sidelined by a hamstring injury. Brooks might be the more dynamic option even if both are healthy, though, and he could be a great value pick in the eighth or ninth round.

Stock down: Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans

Fantasy fans of Pollard will flock to his volume potential. He has neared (and sometimes surpassed) 300 touches each of the past three seasons, and Tennessee might have to lean on its ground game if quarterback Cam Ward can't take a big step forward.

But what happens if Pollard is trapped in a timeshare? Because it kind of seems like the Titans want to up their usage of Tyjae Spears, who has slotted alongside their starters more often than Pollard this preseason. If Pollard is left fighting for touches, then he just isn't worth the draft cost ( RB30 , per FantasPros).

Stock up: De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

Stribling's stock hasn't seen a spike so much as it has perpetually climbed until now. His buzz was building in training camp, and he has kept it moving up with two impressive showings in as many preseason contests, turning 13 targets into 11 receptions for 109 yards.

With Mike Evans struggling to stay on the field, and George Kittle still working his way back from a torn Achilles, Stribling could have a path toward a sizable role in this passing attack. It looks like it might take a top-100 pick to get him, but every sign so far suggests he'll be worth it.

Fantasy managers become their own branding departments when it's time to name the team. Consider us your branding consultants, then, as we'll sift through some options.

If you want something simple that you can carry forward into future campaigns, you can always build the name around your actual name. It isn't the most clever play, but there are no questions about who's in charge of Tommy's Touchdowns or The Zach Attack.

Or maybe you like tailoring it to a standout player on your roster, perhaps your first-round pick. If you're fortunate enough to land Bijan Robinson, then you could use Bijan Mustard, To Infinity and Bijan or Bijan Frisé. Or if you take Christian McCaffrey, Run CMC is always a classic.

Finally, perhaps your prefer to flex some pop culture knowledge. Cleated Rivalry might be right up your alley, then. Or The Trojan Hurts works if you have Jalen Hurts on the roster and enjoyed The Odyssey .

Stribling's stock hasn't seen a spike so much as it has perpetually climbed until now. His buzz was building in training camp, and he has kept it moving up with two impressive showings in as many preseason contests, turning 13 targets into 11 receptions for 109 yards.

With Mike Evans struggling to stay on the field, and George Kittle still working his way back from a torn Achilles, Stribling could have a path toward a sizable role in this passing attack. It looks like it might take a top-100 pick to get him, but every sign so far suggests he'll be worth it.
Fantasy managers become their own branding departments when it's time to name the team. Consider us your branding consultants, then, as we'll sift through some options.

If you want something simple that you can carry forward into future campaigns, you can always build the name around your actual name. It isn't the most clever play, but there are no questions about who's in charge of Tommy's Touchdowns or The Zach Attack.

Or maybe you like tailoring it to a standout player on your roster, perhaps your first-round pick. If you're fortunate enough to land Bijan Robinson, then you could use Bijan Mustard, To Infinity and Bijan or Bijan Frisé. Or if you take Christian McCaffrey, Run CMC is always a classic.

Finally, perhaps your prefer to flex some pop culture knowledge. Cleated Rivalry might be right up your alley, then. Or The Trojan Hurts works if you have Jalen Hurts on the roster and enjoyed The Odyssey .

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers effect: Why a Steelers rookie says sharing the field with him sparks real anxiety
articles.summary: NFL News: Germie Bernard did not arrive at Pittsburgh expecting to feel nervous around his own quarterback. But the Steelers' second-round pick out of Alabama h.
articles.body: Germie Bernard did not arrive at Pittsburgh expecting to feel nervous around his own quarterback. But the Steelers' second-round pick out of Alabama has been refreshingly candid about the pressure of sharing a field with Aaron Rodgers, a 42-year-old playing his final NFL season and clearly not coasting through it. Bernard, selected 47th overall in the 2026 Draft, admitted during the preseason that Rodgers' presence alone puts him on edge in a way no opponent has managed to.Why does Aaron Rodgers make Steelers rookie Germie Bernard so nervous?It is not about fear. It is about wanting to meet the standard of someone who has set the bar impossibly high for over two decades. Bernard put it bluntly: "I'm not going to lie, I be having low-key a little bit of anxiety when I'm out there with him, just because I don't really want to mess up and he finna chew my aâ out."That is the Rodgers effect in plain language. Four MVP awards, a Hall of Fame trajectory, and a reputation for holding everyone around him accountable. For a rookie still learning NFL route timing and defensive tendencies, that kind of proximity to greatness is as motivating as it is terrifying.What makes Bernard's admission interesting is the balance underneath it. He is not complaining. He is not rattled to the point of dysfunction. He added: "At the same time, it's like I enjoy being there with him and being under him because he's just teaching me the game. He's giving me all the knowledge he knows about the game."That dynamic, anxiety sitting right next to gratitude, tells you a lot about how Rodgers is operating this season. Cameras caught him advising Bernard on the sideline during a recent preseason game. That is not the behavior of a quarterback mentally checked out in his final year. Rodgers is invested. He just demands the people around him be invested too.Bernard was productive at Alabama, but college success rarely comes with a guarantee. The NFL asks wider route trees, faster reads, and defenders who get paid specifically to stop you. Having Rodgers in his ear every day of this first season is the kind of football education most rookies never get.Pittsburgh's season likely hinges on whether Bernard and the other young receivers around Rodgers can create separation consistently enough to keep the offense moving. The Steelers fell to Houston in the Wild Card last year. Rodgers wants one more run at something meaningful before he leaves.Bernard's nerves are understandable. But they may also be the making of him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nike y la NFL llevan sus rivalidades históricas a las nuevas camisetas de 2026
articles.standfirst: El programa Rivalries estrena ocho nuevos diseños para los equipos de la NFC North y la AFC South tras convertirse en uno de los grandes éxitos comerciales de la pasada temporada
articles.summary: El programa Rivalries estrena ocho nuevos diseños para los equipos de la NFC North y la AFC South tras convertirse en uno de los grandes éxitos comerciales de la pasada temporada
articles.body: La NFL también juega sus rivalidades fuera del campo. Nike y la liga estadounidense han presentado las nuevas equipaciones de Rivalries para 2026, la segunda temporada de un proyecto que busca trasladar a las camisetas la identidad, historia y orgullo de algunas de las franquicias más reconocibles del campeonato. Este año será el turno de los equipos de la NFC North y la AFC South, con ocho nuevas equipaciones que se estrenarán durante partidos como Green Bay Packers-Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions-Minnesota Vikings o Indianapolis Colts-Houston Texans. Cada uniforme permanecerá durante tres temporadas dentro de la rotación de equipaciones de su franquicia. La apuesta llega después del impacto conseguido en 2025. Según los datos ofrecidos por la organización, el estreno de Rivalries se convirtió en el lanzamiento de merchandising con mayores ventas registrado por Fanatics, un éxito que ha impulsado la expansión del proyecto. Con los ocho conjuntos de la pasada campaña y los ocho que se incorporan ahora, 16 equipos utilizarán diseños Rivalries durante la temporada 2026. Además, Nike y la NFL acompañarán el lanzamiento con campañas protagonizadas por jugadores, leyendas y artistas vinculados a las ciudades de cada franquicia. Las nuevas camisetas y la colección para aficionados saldrán a la venta el próximo 1 de septiembre.

articles.title: NFL, Disney Drop Collaboration with Apparel for All 32 Teams in New Photos Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: The NFL and Disney collaborated to launch new apparel for all 32 teams ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The NFL and Disney collaborated to launch new apparel for all 32 teams ahead of the 2026 season.

The Disney x Champion NFL Collection includes t-shirts and sweatshirts that feature a character from Disney, Pixar, Marvel or Star Wars matched with each team (h/t AL.com's Josie Howell ).

The collection was previously introduced at Fanatics Fest on July 16, with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell helping to showcase the first eight team-character pairings.

Bret Healey, Disney's director of graphic design at Disney Consumer Products, discussed the design process.

"Today's consumers view fandom as an extension of personal style, and this collection was designed with that mindset from the start," Healey said . "Each piece transforms team affiliation into something expressive, collectible and culturally relevant."

The 2026 season will officially kick off when the Seattle Seahawks face the New England Patriots on Sept. 9 at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Ankle Injury Status Discussed by Raiders' Klint Kubiak Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders fans looking for clarity on the severity of Ashton Jeanty's ankle injury didn't get much from head coach Klint Kubiak on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders fans looking for clarity on the severity of Ashton Jeanty's ankle injury didn't get much from head coach Klint Kubiak on Tuesday.

"I'm not gonna get into the injuries," Kubiak told reporters when asked about the running back. "He's on the mend."

He also said , "Ashton got hurt in practice and the whole team took a knee. I think that says a lot about him being on the mend and us counting on him. So, really excited to get him back."

The comments come after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that Jeanty seemed to have avoided a season-ending injury.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

There was significant concern for Jeanty in the immediate aftermath of his setback, especially since Vincent Bonsignore of the California Post reported he couldn't put weight on his leg as he exited the field.

Yet ESPN's Adam Schefter and Rapoport reported it wasn't seen as "a long-term injury" even though there was still some uncertainty regarding the exact timeline.

Considering how secretive some NFL coaches are when it comes to injury updates, Kubiak's comments aren't surprising. He and the Raiders also may not know exactly when the running back will be ready to return to the field at this point.

Las Vegas starts the 2026 campaign on Sept. 13 against the Miami Dolphins.

Jeanty figures to be a major part of its offensive attack after he ran for 975 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie. The Raiders selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft with the hope he would become a franchise building block, and the 2026 campaign represents a chance for him to take a second-year leap.

He has to be on the field to do that, though, which makes the timing of his setback rather concerning even if it isn't a season-ending one.

If Jeanty is out for the game against the Dolphins, look for the Raiders to turn to Mike Washington Jr. at running back.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes says he feels 'great,' still hoping to play in Week 1
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has apparently hit the most optimistic deadlines during his ACL recovery.
articles.body:
When Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes went down with an ACL injury last December, the quarterback seemed likely to miss time early next season. While a quick ACL recovery wasn't necessarily unprecedented, it was rare.

With a few weeks to go before the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, Mahomes said he feels "great" and is still hopeful he'll be able to start in Week 1.

Patrick Mahomes says that his recovery process is going according to plan. He adds, "This has always been the plan. Get me ready for training camp, get all the reps in training camp. Prepare your body so that when you get to week one, you're ready to play the game." pic.twitter.com/ci3cpBsog7 — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) August 25, 2026

Patrick Mahomes says that his recovery process is going according to plan. He adds, "This has always been the plan. Get me ready for training camp, get all the reps in training camp. Prepare your body so that when you get to week one, you're ready to play the game." pic.twitter.com/ci3cpBsog7

Mahomes said he was initially told it would take nine months to recover from his injury. The quarterback underwent surgery Dec. 16, making Sept. 16 exactly nine months since his surgery. The Chiefs are slated to take on the Denver Broncos in Week 1 on Sept. 14, two days before the actual nine-month mark.

That's an aggressive timeline, but one Mahomes said he was always planning to hit.

"This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I'll be able to go out there and be myself."

While that's an encouraging update — as is the fact that Mahomes has been able to take part in team practices — the star quarterback has yet to be cleared to play in games just yet. If that doesn't happen by Friday, Mahomes would miss the entire NFL preseason for the first time in his career.

Even in that case, Mahomes would still have two more weeks to be cleared by team doctors.

NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

If Mahomes is unable to go in Week 1, the Chiefs would likely turn to offseason acquisition Justin Fields for that game. That would represent a pretty steep downgrade for Kansas City to kick off the 2026 regular season.

But in that event, it doesn't sound like the team will need to rely on Fields for long. Mahomes apparently has been able to hit the most optimistic deadlines during his recovery, and should be able to take the field fairly early in the regular season.

As long as he still looks like the Mahomes of old, the Chiefs will have a shot to bounce back and return to contention.

articles.title: Tom Brady Gucci Modeling Photos Revealed as NFL Legend Reflects on 1st Runway Show
articles.summary: NFL legend Tom Brady has traded the gridiron for the runway during his retirement.
articles.body:
NFL legend Tom Brady has traded the gridiron for the runway during his retirement.

In May, the iconic quarterback appeared at a modeling show for Gucci in Times Square, rocking an all-leather look. This week, he got in front of the camera for GQ.

As for whether Brady plans to continue his modeling career in the future, he told GQ that it's not out of the equation.

"I would never say never to doing anything, so if there was an opportunity that presented itself that I thought was really fun and new, I would definitely be open to it," he said. "I always say the only place for growth is outside your comfort zone, and I think this was one of those things: doing something that I had never really done on a big stage with some really great people."

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Gives Week 1 Injury Status Update Amid Knee Rehab as Chiefs Prepare for Broncos
articles.summary: There will likely be a familiar face under center for the Kansas City Chiefs when they open their 2026 campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
There will likely be a familiar face under center for the Kansas City Chiefs when they open their 2026 campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.

Patrick Mahomes told reporters Tuesday he feels like he is on track to start in Week 1 as he continues his recovery from the torn ACL and LCL that ended his 2025 season.

"Being able to go out there, day after day, and have the grind of a camp, that can even be harder than the [regular] season," Mahomes said. "It's been awesome for me to be able to do that. It's exciting. I didn't know if I was going to have to take days off, but my body has responded the right way.

articles.title: Raiders pitch $158 million Allegiant Stadium upgrade with public money
articles.summary: With another Super Bowl on the horizon, the Las Vegas Raiders want to elevate its premier sports venue with a new multi-level event space aimed at tackling h...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are seeking approval for a $158 million upgrade to Allegiant Stadium 's north entrance, including $75 million in public funding. The proposal would add a larger arrival area with pedestrian and event decks, a public plaza, and transportation improvements around the stadium.

The Las Vegas Stadium Authority considered the proposal at its August 20 meeting but did not vote on it. A vote could come September 2, with construction expected to begin after the Raiders' 2026 season. The project is being planned for completion in late 2028 or before the 2029 Super Bowl, which is scheduled to be held at Allegiant Stadium. NFL.com has more details on the proposal and funding plan .

New North Entrance Would Change the Arrival Experience

The proposed project centers on the north side of Allegiant Stadium, where large crowds currently converge after Raiders games and other major events.

The plans include an elevated pedestrian deck, an event deck, a public plaza and improvements to traffic and transportation access. A dedicated rideshare loop would sit beneath the second level, with the goal of making pickups and drop-offs more efficient.

Related: Popular rock band makes major change to Las Vegas Sphere residency

The new entrance would also provide a more direct connection from the Las Vegas Strip, with many fans currently using the nearby Hacienda Avenue bridge to reach the stadium.

Raiders president Sandra Douglass Morgan told the Stadium Authority that the north side has become a pressure point for the guest experience because the existing infrastructure is stretched to capacity.

How the $158 Million Project Would Be Funded

The Raiders are proposing that the Stadium Authority contribute up to $75 million, with the remaining cost covered by the team. The public portion would come from the waterfall residual fund, which is funded by room tax revenue.

The stadium itself opened in 2020 at a reported construction cost of about $2 billion. Public funding contributed to the original project totaled approximately $750 million.

The proposed improvements are intended to prepare the venue for the larger crowds and logistical demands that come with major sporting events and concerts. Allegiant Stadium hosted Super Bowl LVIII in 2024, and the venue is scheduled to host the 2028 Final Four as well as the 2029 Super Bowl.

For now, the project remains a proposal. The Stadium Authority did not take action on August 20, leaving a potential September 2 vote as the next major step.

The Raiders want construction to begin after the 2026 season, with completion targeted for late 2028 or earlier. A successful project would give one of Las Vegas' most prominent sports venues a significantly larger arrival area before it takes on another Super Bowl.

Related: Popular Cirque du Soleil show leaves Las Vegas Strip, refunds available
