articles.title: Dolly Parton Honored by Sports World After Country Music Legend Dies at 80
articles.summary: The world lost an iconic singer-songwriter and country star on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The world lost an iconic singer-songwriter and country star on Tuesday.

Dolly Parton died at 80, her nephew, Bryan Seaver, announced on Instagram.

Following Parton's death, the sports world honored the singer, whose impact stretched well beyond just her music.

Parton's music career spanned nearly 60 years, and she is the best-selling female country music artist of all time, with hits like "I Will Always Love You," "9-5" and "Jolene."

She was born in Sevier County, Tennessee, and went on to become arguably the most famous East Tennessean. She released her first album, "Hello, I'm Dolly," in 1967 and released 48 more solo studio albums, her final being "Rockstar" in 2023.

But Parton's music was just a portion of her extraordinary life.

She opened the Dollywood theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, in 1986, and the park has since become one of the most visited theme parks in the country. As part of the Dollywood Company, she also opened other attractions in the area, like the Dream More Resort and Spa and Dolly Parton's Stampede.

While her philanthropic efforts are immeasurable, Parton's Imagination Library is perhaps the most notable. The program began gifting free books to children in East Tennessee but has since stretched worldwide. Approximately one in six children under the age of five in the United States receives an Imagination Library Book each year.

Parton was a lifelong Tennessee fan and appeared at the Vols' 2023 game against Georgia to perform "Rocky Top," escorted onto the field by legendary quarterback Peyton Manning.

Parton had revealed on social media over the past year that her health began declining in March 2025 following the death of her husband, Carl Dean, with the most recent update coming last week.

articles.title: New research finds 1 in 4 NFL players could develop CTE in their lifetime: 'Should be a call to action'
articles.summary: A new study found at least one in four former NFL players may develop CTE, prompting Dr. Julian Bailes to call for urgent proactive brain protection.
articles.body: The NFL continues to make a concerted effort for safe play for all players, especially when it comes to head injuries. But since chronic traumatic encephalopathy, better known as CTE, was found to be heavily linked to former professional football players, there has been ongoing discussion about how current and future NFL players could be affected. New data published in The BMJ from a recent six-year research period provided some harrowing discoveries. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! The study found that at least one in every four people who have played in the NFL might expect to end up with CTE at some point in their lives. For the study, 878 former NFL players who died from 2016-21, which varied from players in their 20s to their 80s and in between, at least 215 of them had CTE in some stage. That’s 24.5%, with the actual prevalence likely being higher considering there were 643 of those brains that were not examined. ALDON SMITH'S FAMILY DONATING HIS BRAIN TO CTE RESEARCH AS ATTORNEYS INVESTIGATE DEATH If these results were applied to the NFL today, which consists of 1,696 players on the active roster combined for all 32 teams — this doesn’t include practice squad players and those not on the roster due to other injury reasons — around 415 would be diagnosed with CTE. One of the main problems of the degenerative brain disease is that it can only be confirmed as a diagnosis post-death once the brain is examined. The neurodegenerative disease is caused by repeated blows to the head as well as severe head trauma. The symptoms found in those with CTE include memory loss, mood swings, erratic behavioral actions and more. While the disease was first found in boxers, it has become associated with football players in this modern era due to the repeated blows to the head sustained on every snap of the ball. It has, however, also been found in athletes participating in hockey, rugby and other sports. But its connection to football became public when beloved players like Junior Seau, Mike Webster, Frank Gifford and others were diagnosed with CTE after their deaths. Webster was dubbed "Patient Zero" after Dr. Bennet Omalu examined his brain and became the first to diagnose an NFL player with CTE, jump-starting a concussion crisis within the game. Dr. Julian Bailes, a neurosurgeon and chief medical advisor for Q-30 Sports Science, has spent decades studying the disease as well as concussion and repetitive subconcussive impacts. He helped pioneer the early investigation into CTE, being portrayed by Alec Baldwin in the popular film, "Concussion." He has also authored more than 300 publications and previously advised the NFL Players Association, NCAA and Pop Warner Football. Seeing this study, Dr. Bailes believes it "should be a call to action for everyone involved in football." SUPER BOWL CHAMPION STEVE MCMICHAEL, WHO DIED LAST YEAR, REVEALED TO HAVE CTE "We have made tremendous progress in recognizing and managing concussions, but the science increasingly tells us that diagnosed concussions are only part of the equation," Dr. Bailes said in a statement provided to OutKick. "Repetitive head impacts accumulated over years of play matter, and we need to bring the same urgency we’ve applied to understanding CTE to preventing and reducing the forces experienced by the brain in the first place. "That means continuing to advance rules, training, equipment and new approaches to brain protection at every level of the game. This should not be approached as an all or nothing assignment. The next frontier in athlete safety must be proactive brain protection." A simple proactive action would be eliminating repeated blows to the head, which researchers know prevents CTE. Obviously, the game of football would forever be changed and there’s much more complexities there, especially at the professional level. "The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts," the league told The Athletic in a statement. "The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental well being." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The NFL Players Association also told the outlet, "The finds should serve as a call to action across the entire football ecosystem." There were 168 documented in-game concussions during the 2025 NFL season, which was a 30% increase from the 129 record during the 2024 campaign. There were a total of 538 evaluations and 26 medical timeouts as well.

articles.title: Peyton Manning pays tribute to Dolly Parton: 'Tennessee won't be the same without her!'
articles.summary: Peyton Manning shared a heartfelt tribute to Dolly Parton, reflecting on their Tennessee connection and her iconic 2023 Vols "Rocky Top" performance.
articles.body: Tributes, condolences and more are pouring in after news of country music legend Dolly Parton’s death at 80 surfaced on Tuesday. Among those was Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning, who shared a connection with Parton given their ties to Tennessee. "There was only one Dolly and I feel lucky to have known her," Manning, who played his college football at the University of Tennessee, wrote in an Instagram post walking alongside Parton at a Vols game. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! "We’ll miss you, Dolly. Tennessee won’t be the same without her!" The picture that Manning posted was one of many iconic performances for Parton, but this one was exceptionally good by the East Tennessee native. She performed the Vols’ signature "Rocky Top" song after the first quarter on Nov. 18, 2023. STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING Parton even said that she could barely hear herself during her performance because the stadium was so loud. But Parton’s moments in sports went well beyond appearances at Vols games. Just days after her performance in Knoxville, Parton was in Dallas at AT&T Stadium for a 2023 Thanksgiving performance, wearing a custom bedazzled Cowboys cheerleader outfit for the halftime show. She was 77 years old at the time, and rave reviews poured in about her country music ensemble, which included hits like "Jolene," "9 to 5," and even tossing in Queen’s iconic "We Are The Champions" track. "Well at my age, if I can pull it off, it’s going to be good," Parton told USA TODAY about the performance, which she admitted being nervous for. "And if I don’t, I can just pass it off as an old woman doing a stupid thing. I’ve always said my desire to do something is greater than my fear of it." Parton died peacefully in Nashville, Tennessee, on Tuesday, according to a press release obtained by Fox News Digital. Her nephew, Brin Seaver, also revealed the news in an Instagram video, which comes after Parton spent months battling an unknown health issue. Parton was much more than a country music artist, as she was known for also being an actress, a philanthropist, a businesswoman and humanitarian. During her illustrious life and career, Parton tallied 11 Grammy Awards, three Emmy Awards, and the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award, while also being nominated for six Golden Globe Awards, a Tony Award and two Academy Awards. Parton was also married to Carl Dean for nearly 60 years, with their relationship mostly remaining outside the public eye. Dean passed away in March 2025. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP At Parton’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family. In lieu of flowers, the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library. Fox News’ Christian Dugan Ramirez contributed to this report.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick to receive Muhammad Ali Award for fighting 'racial injustice'
articles.summary: Colin Kaepernick will receive the Muhammad Ali Center's Humanitarian of the Year Award, but comparing his NFL anthem protest to Ali's sacrifices misses.
articles.body: Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick will receive the Muhammad Ali Center’s Humanitarian of the Year Award later this year. The center told Reuters that it selected Kaepernick for his advocacy "against racial injustice" and support for underserved communities through his Know Your Rights Camp and other philanthropic efforts. Lonnie Ali, Muhammad’s late wife and co-founder of the center, added: "Colin has used his platform to advocate for equality, human dignity, and social change, even when doing so came at significant personal and professional cost." STOP COMPARING JAXSON DART'S NEW YORK TRUMP RALLY SPEECH TO COLIN KAEPERNICK'S ACTIVISM Now, to reality. Kaepernick is hardly worthy of an award bearing Muhammad Ali’s name. Ali risked his freedom and sacrificed the prime of his boxing career when he refused induction into the military during the Vietnam War. He was stripped of his heavyweight title, barred from boxing for more than three years and convicted of draft evasion. Ali became a martyr. He paid a real price. Kaepernick did neither. The popular narrative that Kaepernick sacrificed a thriving NFL career to stand up for marginalized communities is misleading. He had already been benched for Blaine Gabbert. In his final two seasons, he posted QBRs of 43.7 and 49.2. VICTOR WEMBANYAMA CROSSING HIS ARMS DURING U.S. NATIONAL ANTHEM IS A PROBLEM FOR THE NBA He had become unplayable. Unlike Ali, Kaepernick was not on a battlefield alone. It was quite the opposite. Sports media and pop culture largely championed his national anthem protests. Nike made him the face of a major advertising campaign Kneeling during the anthem proved financially rewarding for an athlete who would've had to otherwise settle for league minimum contracts. Kaepernick and his defenders say the NFL blackballed him. In reality, no team wanted a backup-quality quarterback attached to a divisive political circus. Most players who kneeled during the anthem kept their jobs because their play warranted it. Kaepernick’s did not. He had also become an inflammatory figure, denouncing July 4 as a racist celebration and comparing the NFL’s treatment of players to slavery and plantations. Colin Kaepernick was more moron than martyr. The Muhammad Ali Center should be ashamed to honor him. Then again, the center lost much of its prestige years ago. In 2022, it awarded Dr. Anthony Fauci its Lifetime Achievement Award. Oh, how poorly that has aged. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Still, Kaepernick will use the award to promote his upcoming book, "The Perilous Fight."

articles.title: NFL trades: 3 roster positions the Browns should be looking to upgrade
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry could see the trade rumor mill spin up as the 53-man roster has some needs
articles.body:
While NFL free agency is ongoing until the end of the Super Bowl, the Cleveland Browns and the rest of the NFL are mostly scraping the bottom of the barrel at this point in time in the season. Sure, RB Kareem Hunt might be able to help a team like the Detroit Lions , and the Browns are hoping that DE Derek Barnett helps offset the loss of DE Alex Wright , but there are reasons that players are still available on the NFL free-agent market.

NFL trade rumors could start to swirl as teams prepare for cutdown day, with Cleveland's Thursday Night contest giving them a bit of a head start . If the free agent market doesn't have answers, teams may look to swap positions of depth to help fill positions of weakness before starting preparation for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season.

A look at a 53-man roster projection for the Browns seems to indicate some obvious holes that could be filled on the trade market. Three positions stand out with depth concerns:

Harold Fannin Jr. is a great young starting point, but after that, Cleveland is looking at a career journeyman ( Blake Whiteheart ) and a late-round rookie ( Carsen Ryan ) to fill the rest of the depth chart. The NFL is not full of a lot of tight ends ready to play meaningful snaps who are also available in a trade, but GM Andrew Berry will likely make some calls.

Berry has been looking for edge help since training camp started, with Barnett coming in to offset Wright's injury. Any and every defensive end that could hit the waiver wire or free agent market might instead end up on the Browns roster via a trade.

With Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell , Cleveland's cornerback room is set at the top. The Browns seem convinced that Myles Harden can handle the slot corner spot but, beyond that, there are a lot of questions. DC Mike Rutenberg could end up playing a lot of three safeties to offset the corner need if Berry can't bring in any help.

Besides quarterback, which has been the big conversation all offseason, where do you have the most concern on the Browns roster and do you expect them to fill it with a trade?

articles.title: TE Dae’Quan Wright’s story takes another turn; may not be done with Browns, NFL after all
articles.summary: Dae’Quan Wright’s story could end up with him back with the Cleveland Browns instead of at LSU based on SEC’s policy
articles.body:
For a player who went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft and was waived by the Philadelphia Eagles before being claimed by the Cleveland Browns , TE Dae'Quan Wright has become a big name in the story of football. While one of our astute readers was very excited when the Browns claimed Wright , his odds of making the team's initial 53-man roster were low, but the lack of depth at his position might have helped.

Instead, Wright was a part of a lawsuit that deemed he could return to college , despite another legal ruling seemingly stopping that, and was waived by Cleveland to make a "history" making move to LSU possible . On Tuesday, Wright cleared waivers and was set to join Lane Kiffin's Tigers:

As the immortal Lee Corso would say, "Not so fast, my friends."

The SEC joined the Big 10 in passing a policy that would lead to LSU receiving penalties if they had Wright, or any other player who met the three provisions of the policy, on their roster:

Following meetings with the Presidents, Chancellors, and Athletics Directors of the Southeastern Conference, the SEC will enforce the following policy: pic.twitter.com/LohWnb7G1J — Southeastern Conference (@SEC) August 25, 2026

Following meetings with the Presidents, Chancellors, and Athletics Directors of the Southeastern Conference, the SEC will enforce the following policy: pic.twitter.com/LohWnb7G1J

As former Green Bay Packers executive Andrew Brandt is fond of saying, "There will be lawyers."

As for Wright returning to the Browns, anything is possible, as he is now an NFL (and potentially college) free agent. Given the timing, even if Wright signs with an NFL team, it is highly unlikely to be on a 53-man roster; instead, the athletic tight end would likely end up on a practice squad.

Then again, Wright's story has already had lots of twists and turns; perhaps he tries to transfer to a school in a conference that hasn't yet passed a rule like the Big 10 and SEC. Given the wild swings so far, a return to Cleveland is likely an option as well.

What do you think of all of this? Is it just a blip on the radar or a bigger issue for football in general?

articles.title: Detroit Lions host RB Kareem Hunt, try out two cornerbacks
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions hosted former Pro Bowl running back Kareem Hunt, while trying out a pair of defensive backs.
articles.body:
In one of the more fascinating visits to Allen Park, the Detroit Lions hosted former Pro Bowl running Kareem Hunt at the team facility on Tuesday, per the NFL transaction list.

Hunt was a third-round pick in 2017 and immediately put together an impressive rookie season with the Kansas City Chiefs , rushing for 1,327 yards, eight touchdowns, and 4.9 yards per carry. Unfortunately for Hunt, that would turn out to be his best career season. He has since dealt with several injuries and an ugly off-field incident where video surfaced of him assaulting a 19-year-old girl. He was promptly released by the Chiefs less than two years into his career, but never faced criminal charges.

Since then, Hunt spent five seasons with the Browns before returning to the Chiefs in 2024. He has had three seasons where he eclipsed 700 rushing yards (2018, 2020, 2024) and is coming off a pretty strong season in which he somewhat ironically outpaced new Lions running back Isiah Pacheco . In 2024, Hunt rushed for 611 yards, 3.7 yards per carry, and eight touchdowns. Pacheco only managed 462 yards and a single rushing touchdown despite starting 12 games.

The reasoning for the Lions' presumed interest in Hunt is not entirely clear. Detroit did recently lose two running backs in their latest preseason game. Raheem Blackshear was placed on injured reserved and promptly released with an injury settlement, while Jabari Small suffered a concussion against the Commanders . The Lions still have Jahmyr Gibbs , Sione Vaki , Jacob Saylors , Trayveon Williams and newly signed Roydell Williams healthy, but they may not want to play most of those players in their preseason finale on Saturday.

The one unknown is the health of presumed RB2 Isiah Pacheco. The veteran running back has been sidelined with an MCL sprain, but at the time, coach Dan Campbell said they weren't fearful of that threatening his start to the regular season.

"We feel pretty good about him being ready to go, certainly when the season gets here," Campbell said two weeks ago. "So, I'm not concerned about that."

On top of that, the Lions also hosted two cornerbacks for a tryout: Shaun Jolly and Eric Scott. Jolly went undrafted out of Appalachian State in 2022 and spent three seasons with the Rams —appearing in six games—before losing his entire 2025 season to injury. At 5-foot-9, 180 pounds, Jolly has some versatility to play on the outside and inside.

Scott is more of a pure outside cornerback at 6-foot-2, 197 pounds. He has yet to make his first NFL appearance since being drafted by the Cowboys in the sixth round back in 2023, but he's spent time on both Dallas ' and Kansas City 's practice squad.

articles.title: Updates on Bud Clark's Broken Ankle Injury and Timeline for Star Rookie to Return to Seahawks
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks rookie safety Bud Clark is out for the 2026 season after suffering a broken ankle during Sunday's preseason game against the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks rookie safety Bud Clark is out for the 2026 season after suffering a broken ankle during Sunday's preseason game against the Tennessee Titans.

Seattle placed Clark on injured reserve on Tuesday, ending his campaign before it even began.

Clark, 24, was a second-round pick by the Seahawks in April out of TCU.

Clark, 24, was battling to earn the starting free safety job following Coby Bryant's departure during the offseason. Ty Okada has topped the team's depth chart at the position during summer, joining Julian Love.

The status of Nick Emmanwori is also very much up in the air due to ankle issues, leaving the Seahawks a bit thin in the secondary:

Clark, meanwhile, spent six seasons at TCU, accumulating 214 tackles, 15 interceptions, one sack, one fumble recovery and one defensive touchdown.

NFL.com's Lance Zierlein compared him to Kerby Joseph in his scouting report, noting that his "traits won't pop but his tape most certainly will. Clark is a coverage-versatile safety in a cornerback's body with the talent to range over the top or man up on the slot. He plays with an overriding desire to do everything all at once—which produces spectacular takeaways and occasional breakdowns—but the good outweighs the bad."

Unfortunately, his rookie season is now over after the serious ankle injury.
